How to run this in Claude Design

  1. Publish the Pantopus design system in Claude Design

    Claude Design reads design systems as published, org-level objects. It does not document opening another project from a share link, so don't rely on the two share links for that. A “Pantopus” design system was already extracted from this repo on 16 Sep: Pantopus design system (107 colours in 3 themes, 33 text styles, spacing, radius and shadow tokens, and 50 real web components). You can rebuild it with node tools/design-system/build.mjs. Use it as the source, and make sure the design system Claude Design uses carries real material, not just specs:
    • the token files: frontend/packages/theme/src/ (colors, typography, spacing, radii, shadows, css-variables), iOS Core/Design/, Android ui/theme/ and web globals.css plus tailwind.config.js
    • your two existing Pantopus Claude Design projects (export them and upload, or publish them if they already are the system)
    • screenshots of today's core screens (Place, Today, Nearby and Mail on web, iOS and Android)
    Then switch Published on. Every project you create from the homescreen after that uses it automatically.

  2. Design the Foundations first: four projects, one per board

    Create a project for each board (00a, 00b, 00c, 00d). In each one, paste the house style, send the board's setup prompt, and wait for “ready”. Then send one component prompt per turn, typing “continue” between artboard batches. When you accept a component, add it to the design system under its exact name. These 36 components are how 59 separately designed screens come out identical.

  3. Then the screens, one project per screen, in build order

    Create each project from the homescreen. Paste the house style, then the screen prompt. Attach the screenshots listed under Attach: for an Extend prompt, the existing screen is the source of truth. Claude Design draws at most 6 artboards per turn; reply “continue” to get the next batch. Batch 1 holds the must-have frames. The later batches cover the remaining states, platforms, large text, greyscale and dark mode.

  4. Export after every batch you accept

    Claude Design has no version history yet, so export HTML or PDF into docs/design/exports/<prompt-id>/ each time. The journey storyboards attach these exports.

  5. Last, the journey storyboards

    Each storyboard lays out finished screens as one connected journey, so you can see where the handoffs break: what is carried across, what the person sees at each moment of truth, and where each failure branch goes. Fix what they reveal in the screen projects.

  6. Review every artboard against the same checklist

    Text contrast is at least 4.5:1 and graphics at least 3:1. Targets are 44pt / 48dp. Provenance marks mean official / on record, not confirmed / you added this, and nothing else. The only scope strings are “Saved place · Only you” and “Your household”. Silence shows its receipt. No percentages, streaks or confetti. It reads correctly in greyscale and at the largest text size. Give element-level feedback with inline comments; ask for 2–3 options only where the form is genuinely open.

House style

2,057 words · paste first in every project

This block is the contract every project starts from: the product, the user, the platforms, the four tabs, concrete visual specs, tokens and how to use them, the shared fixtures, the six invariants, accessibility, microcopy, push rules, motion, the artboard convention, and what to avoid.

PANTOPUS HOUSE STYLE v2. Paste once per project, then the surface prompt.

PRODUCT. Pantopus: "See what's true about your address." Type an address and see what is on public record (flood, wildfire, air, radon, pickup, civic deadlines). Save it privately, claim it as your home, then verify it. It works with zero other users: a night-before pickup push, a briefing that stays silent unless a threshold is crossed, a widget, important dates, and co-residents sharing calendar and bills.
USER. People who just moved, aged about 25 to 70, busy, some using large text. Pilot: Camas and Vancouver, WA, on web, iOS and Android.
PLATFORMS. Web 1440x900 (left sidebar) and 390x844 (bottom tab bar). iOS 393x852, native navigation, sheets with detents. Android 412x915, Material 3, bottom sheets. Widgets on 393x852: 158x158, 338x158 and 338x354pt, with 16pt margins.
NAVIGATION. Exactly four tabs: Place · Today · Nearby · Mail. There is no fifth tab or FAB. Tab labels are always visible. Every screen is reached from a tab or a deep link. Tab icons as shipped: Place a house, Today a sun, Nearby a compass, Mail an envelope on iOS and web; Android draws Today as a cloud with sun, Nearby as a map pin and Mail as a mailbox.

DESIGN SYSTEM. This project uses the published "Pantopus" design system. Attached host screenshots are exact: change only what the prompt lists.
Human reference, same source of truth (do not rely on opening these by link): https://claude.ai/design/p/019e16cb-d2a9-77b0-b9e0-370dbe3856ba?via=share · https://claude.ai/design/p/c65a37ac-191a-4cdc-9f30-602926979fd6?via=share. Match existing screens; no new card style, type scale or icon set.
COMPONENTS: see the Foundations board (prompt 00) — use these by exact name.
LOGO: the Pantopus logo is attached to this first message: pantopus-logo-lockup.png (mark and wordmark, for light grounds), pantopus-logo-mark.png and pantopus-logo-mark-dark.png. Use them wherever a screen shows the logo; on dark grounds, put the dark mark beside the wordmark set in dark text.primary. Never draw a placeholder mark.

VISUAL SPECS (concrete, not mood). Type: the platform system sans only: SF Pro on iOS (Dynamic Type), Roboto on Android, and the system-ui stack on web (ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto). Use no serif display type and no italic accents. Backgrounds are surface.app, base or raised only. Never use cream, paper or tinted backgrounds. SCOPE NOTE: the marketing homepage (/) alone uses a serif display face on paper backgrounds. Keep that as-is on the homepage and nowhere else. Radii: xs 4 · sm 6 · md 8 (inputs) · lg 12 (buttons) · xl 16 (info notes, toasts) · 2xl (THE card radius: every section card, row card and sheet) · 3xl (large marketing panels) · pill. 2xl is 20 on every platform (web rounded-2xl is 20px in this codebase, not Tailwind's default 16); use the token, never a number. (The Foundations boards draw their specimen containers at radius lg: that is board chrome, not a product card.) Spacing: 4px base (4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64). Elevation: shadow sm (y1, blur 3, 4%) for cards, md (y2, blur 6, 6%) for raised controls, lg for sheets. Warmth comes from the copy voice and primary.50 selected fills, not from colour. Use only the type scale below and never invent sizes.

TOKENS (always by name, never raw hex)
  Primary sky ramp 50-900 · DEFAULT #0284c7 · 500 #0ea5e9 · 700 #0369a1 · 800
  Surfaces: base #FFFFFF · raised #F9FAFB · sunken #F3F4F6 · app #F6F7F9 · muted #F8FAFC
  Text: primary #111827 · strong #374151 · secondary #4e5563 · muted #5f6775 · inverse #FFFFFF
  Borders: default #E5E7EB · strong #D1D5DB · focus #0284c7 · subtle #F3F4F6
  Semantic: success #047857/#F0FDF4 · warning #9a4a08/#FFFBEB · error #a81a1a/#FEF2F2 · info #0369a1/#F0F9FF
  Dark semantic (same token, dark value): success #34D399 · warning #FBBF24 · error #F87171
  Pillars (color-identity-*): personal #0369A1 · home #15803D · business #7C3AED · dark: personal #38BDF8 · home #4ADE80 · business #A78BFA. #16A34A is color-brand-check, the verification tick only. There is no professional pillar token.
  Dark: base #0F172A · raised #1E293B · app #020617 · text primary #E5E7EB · secondary #94A3B8 · muted #8b98ac · border #1F2937 · focus/link #38BDF8
  THREE themes ship: Light, Dark (web) and Dark · iOS (the asset catalog, slightly warmer: text #e6edf3, surface #161b22, bg #0d1117). Draw Light and Dark; Dark · iOS follows the same structure.
  Type: h1 30/36/700 · h2 24/32/600 · h3 20/28/600 · body 16/24/400 · bodySmall 14/20/400 · label 13/18 · caption 12/16/400 · overline 11/16/600 caps +0.5
HOUSE RULE: every colour is a semantic token; the codebase forbids hex literals in Features/**. If a colour isn't listed, use the nearest token.
TOKEN USAGE. The published design system's tokens.json is the authority: read the token, never hard-code a hex. The semantic inks were darkened in September 2026 to pass AA on light surfaces, so measured contrast is now text.secondary 7.49:1 on base (6.81 on sunken), text.muted 5.70:1, error 7.43:1, warning 6.26:1, success 5.48:1. text.muted still means placeholder and disabled only: that is a meaning rule, not a contrast one. Filled buttons and inline links use primary.700 (in dark mode, links use #38BDF8). Semantic hues go on glyphs and borders only; text on a semantic tint is text.primary. Border tokens are decoration and never the only edge of a band, segment, mark or input; those edges use ink at text.secondary strength or darker. In dark mode, menus, popovers and sheets sit on dark surface.raised with a 1px dark border.strong edge, never on the fill of the card beneath, so their edge stays visible.
The one colour exception: the AQI track uses EPA ColorVision Assist hues (Green 158,255,145 · Yellow 255,201,5 · Orange 255,130,5 · Red 240,34,0 · Purple 137,9,151 · Maroon 100,0,21), with 2px surface gaps between segments, a keyline, and a two-tone marker.

INVARIANTS (product decisions; do not reopen them)
  1. Unverified looks unverified. Provenance marks: FILLED = official or confirmed; HOLLOW = on record, not confirmed; FILLED WITH A KNOCKED-OUT TICK = you added it. Marks are at least 12pt with a stroke of at least 1.5px and at least 3:1 contrast. Each surface shows the matching word once (a legend or first-occurrence label). Standalone surfaces (widget, push, share card) print the word next to the mark. Filled vs hollow means provenance and nothing else.
  2. Scope is always stated with one of two strings: "Saved place · Only you" or "Your household". Scope changes need an explicit choice.
  3. No claims about a neighbour's home. Describe places and datasets, never people's houses.
  4. Silence is a designed state. "Nothing needs your attention today" appears only when every check succeeded; show the receipt ("Checked 6:00 PM · weather · air · alerts · your calendar"). A failed check names the provider and offers Retry.
  5. Sources are shown as a caption: authority · scope · as-of.
  6. No grades, scores, percentages, verdicts, radar charts, rainbow ramps, streaks, completion fractions or confetti.

ACCESSIBILITY. Text contrast is at least 4.5:1 and meaningful graphics at least 3:1, in light, dark and Increase Contrast. The one pair that still fails is white on primary.600 (4.10:1), so filled buttons and inline links use primary.700 (5.93:1). Tap targets are 44pt on iOS, 48dp on Android with 8dp gaps, and 44px on web; a small mark is never a target by itself (its row or cell is). Never use colour alone; every frame must still read correctly in greyscale, so text links are underlined. Charts, strips and bands get a one-sentence summary, a spoken label and a list of the same facts. No action is gesture-only or hover-only. Every sheet has a visible Close or Done and does not stack on another sheet. Undo stays available until the user leaves the screen: no countdowns. Selection must look different from focus. Sticky bars reserve scroll padding. At AX5 or 200% text, pairs stack, text wraps instead of truncating, and sheets may scroll. Orientation is never locked.

MICROCOPY. Write at a grade 6 to 8 reading level, in sentence case. Buttons start with a verb ("Add a date", "Change pickup day"). Declines are neutral and equal weight ("Not now", "Skip", "Just me"). Plain meaning comes first, then the code: "Zone X — minimal flood hazard". Say "hazard" or "potential" as the authority does; never write "100-year flood". Pair a word with a number: "Moderate · 3 of 5". Dates show the weekday: "Mon 26 Oct"; beyond tomorrow, add the relative count: "in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct". A date never breaks across lines: keep "Fri 28 Aug" together (non-breaking spaces) and let the line break at the " · " before it. Deadlines say "must arrive by". Never write "midnight". No "Oops", no "Are you sure?", no "Congratulations". Error text says what to do next.
PUSH. Titles are 30 characters or fewer, with the caveat first: "Unconfirmed: pickup tomorrow". Bodies are 40 characters or fewer, with no house number and no amounts. Never "Open Pantopus to…".

MOTION AND HAPTICS. Motion must have a purpose and last 300ms or less; idle loops stop within 5s. Reduce Motion: cross-fades and static poses, no shimmer. Deep-link landings scroll once and fade a highlight. Haptics: one light tick on confirm only.

ARTBOARDS. Name each artboard "<surface-id> · <ios|android|web-390|web-1440> · <NN-state> · <light|dark>" and show that name as a visible label above the frame. Priority order: the dense default, then the states that change layout, then empty/loading/error/offline, then platform variants, then AX5/200% and greyscale, then the dark twins listed in the prompt. Deliver at most about 6 artboards per turn, following the prompt's BATCH PLAN, and wait for "continue". The last artboard is Notes: assumptions, invented strings, omitted states. Ask a question only if two readings would give materially different screens.

AVOID (research-backed)
  Permission asks at launch, or a primer button labelled "Allow"/"Yes" · tours and asks in modals · "Not now" that asks again · retyping a held value · full-page spinners · an all-clear shown early · stale data replaced by a blank · text on AQI fills · per-cell targets in strips · re-sorting compare rows · warning-tinted countdowns on perks · creature guilt or distress · keeper or marketing pushes · Time Sensitive for pickup · custom Android share choosers · text-heavy OG images · "Add it for me" on iOS.

WHAT THIS BOARD IS FOR
The first design work for Pantopus, before any screen. It draws nine components once, precisely, with every variant and state: ProvenanceMark · SourceCaption · ScopeChip · FreshnessLine · OfflineNotice · StatusChip · KindGlyph · AddressChip · ChoiceChip. Every later screen is designed in a separate project with no memory of this one and uses these exact names, so label everything with its name, keys (B12) and tokens.

HOW THIS PROJECT RUNS
- The board rules (B1–B17) and the Notes rules below apply to every artboard in this project.
- Next, I send one component message per turn, in order. Each one opens with "Component 00a-NN: <Name>." and carries that component's specification, its ARTBOARDS list and its BATCH PLAN.
- A long component arrives in parts (for example 00a-NNa, then 00a-NNb). A part message takes the place of "continue" and carries the specification for the next batch. Specifications from earlier parts of the same component still apply.
- Draw only the current batch (at most 6 artboards), in the listed order. Then stop and wait for "continue", the next part or the next component message. If a batch will not fit, finish the artboards in order and say which ones moved to the next turn.
- Everything you need is in this message and the current component message (with its earlier parts). Components already drawn here are final; reuse them exactly when embedded. Never rely on any other project, file or link.
- Where a component message differs from a board rule, it wins for that component only, and the difference goes on Notes.

PUBLISH (a founder step; you only prepare the index)
When the founder accepts a component, the founder adds it to the published Pantopus design system under its exact name, so it comes out identical on all 59 later surfaces. Make this mechanical: list every specimen name on 00a · Notes, section E. Give one name per drawn grid cell, plus one for each anatomy size or platform form the component message lists under PUBLISH KEYS. "Does not apply" cells get no name.
  <Component> / <variant> / <state> / <size|platform> / <light|dark>
<variant> and <state> are exactly the printed keys (B12), never the labels. The <size|platform> slot takes exactly one of these strings: size codes in uppercase (XS, S, M, L, OG); platform codes in lowercase (ios, android, web); otherwise "any". It is "any" unless the component message says otherwise. Example: "StatusChip / overdue / default / any / light".

======================================================================
BOARD RULES
======================================================================

B1. Artboards. Every artboard is 1440 px wide and as tall as its content needs, on surface.app (light) or dark surface.app (dark). A component message may set a wider artboard for a grid (for example 2000 or 2400 px); that message gives the margins, label column and gutters, and records the width on Notes, section A. Name each artboard "00a · <Component> · <NN-state> · <light|dark>". The component name takes the house style's platform slot, because one specimen artboard shows all three platforms. The only other artboard is "00a · Notes". Print each exact name above its frame in label 13/18/600 text.strong. The standard kinds are:
  01-anatomy: callouts, TOKEN AND CONTRAST TABLE, ACCESSIBILITY, COPY, PLATFORMS, INSTEAD OF.
  02-variants-states (light and dark): the variant × state grid.
  03-scaling-greyscale: AX5, 200% and web zoom frames, GREYSCALE and INCREASE CONTRAST.
  04-in-context: crops of real surfaces. Label each crop with its surface id, platform, width and fixture (Home A, Place B or Friend C).
The component message lists its exact artboards and any extra dark twins.

B2. Top block. Inside each component artboard, print the component name in h1 30/36/700 text.primary, its one-line purpose in body 16/24 text.secondary, then "Used in:" plus the line the message gives, in caption 12/16 text.secondary, exactly. Each section below gets an overline 11/16/600 caps heading (ANATOMY, GREYSCALE and so on).

B3. Specimen cells. Draw each specimen on a surface.base card (radius lg 12, shadow sm, 16 px padding) unless the cell names another surface. Under the card, print its cell label in caption 12/16 text.secondary: its keys, size and surface, joined by " · ". Example: "official · default · S 16pt · on surface.base".

B4. Callouts. Draw 1 px text.secondary leader lines that end in a numbered SQUARE badge (16×16, radius xs 4, surface.sunken fill, label 13/18/600 text.strong numeral). Beside each number, give the measurement and token in caption 12/16 text.strong, for example "[1] 12pt disc · ink text.secondary". Badges are square because circles are reserved (B8). Callout numbers written [1]–[7] or ①–⑦ in a component message are these square badges; never draw them as circles. Dimension lines are 1 px text.secondary with 4 px end ticks and the number centred.

B5. Units and sizes. The first time a size appears in a section, give it three ways: "16pt / 16dp / 16px" (iOS / Android / web; the values are equal). Spacing uses only 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48 and 64. Type uses only the type scale, the large-text sizes in B9, and any deviation a message records on Notes. Any other dimension is allowed only where this setup or a component message states it.

B6. Tokens by name, and dark mode. Label every colour by its token name. Hex values appear only in each TOKEN AND CONTRAST TABLE; the values below are for you. Dark artboards use:
  surface.base #FFFFFF → dark surface.base #0F172A
  surface.raised #F9FAFB → dark surface.raised #1E293B
  surface.sunken #F3F4F6 → dark surface.sunken #0F172A (same as dark base)
  surface.app #F6F7F9 → dark surface.app #020617
  surface.muted #F8FAFC → dark surface.muted #111827
  text.primary #111827 → dark text.primary #E5E7EB
  text.strong #374151 → dark text.strong #F1F5F9
  text.secondary #6B7280 → dark text.secondary #94A3B8
  text.muted #9CA3AF → dark text.muted #64748B (disabled controls and placeholders only)
  border.default #E5E7EB → dark border.default #1F2937 (decoration only)
  border.strong #D1D5DB → dark border.strong #374151 (decoration only)
  border.focus #0284c7 → dark border.focus #38BDF8
  primary.700 #0369a1 (links, selected text, selected edges) → "primary.400 (dark link)" #38BDF8, the same value as dark border.focus. Use that exact name on the board.
  primary.50 #f0f9ff (selected fill) → primary.900 #0c4a6e with dark text.primary on it. primary.400 (dark link) on primary.900 is for glyphs and edges only.
  primary.500 #0ea5e9 appears only where a component message names it.
  semantic.success #059669, semantic.warning #D97706 and semantic.error #DC2626 keep their hue in dark mode and go on glyphs only. primary.700 stands in for semantic.info where a message says so.
  Sunken fills: dark surface.sunken equals dark surface.base, so a sunken fill vanishes on a dark base card. Use dark surface.sunken on dark surface.raised, and dark surface.raised on dark surface.base or dark surface.app. These fills need no border.

B7. Contrast numbers. Ratios are WCAG 2 ratios computed from the real tokens. A colour at an opacity is alpha-blended over its surface in sRGB with unrounded channels, and every ratio is rounded to 2 decimals at the end. Each component message's TOKEN AND CONTRAST TABLE gives the figures that component needs. Print them exactly as given, and do not recompute them.

B8. Circles are reserved. Only ProvenanceMark may draw a solid disc, a ring, or a disc with a knocked-out tick. This covers any glyph silhouette and any drawn dot, bullet or badge. The typographic middle dot (·) in text is allowed. Round sub-parts inside a larger glyph are fine (a head, cart wheels, a pin's hole). Draw dot groups inside a glyph as short dashes or small rounded squares. The only other exceptions are the platform radio indicators that a component message names and flags on Notes. No iOS or web frame draws an unselected radio ring; the only ring in those frames is ProvenanceMark's unconfirmed mark.

B9. Large text. AX5 frames (iOS, 393 wide): caption 40pt, label 44pt, bodySmall 46pt, body 53pt. Android 200% frames (412 wide): caption 24sp, label 26sp, bodySmall 28sp, body 32sp. Crop both frames to the component and its row. Pairs stack, text wraps and never ends in an ellipsis, pills that must wrap become rounded rectangles (radius lg 12), and hit areas grow. Glyphs and marks scale with their text, capped at 2× their default size; a component message states any size that does not scale. Web 200% zoom frames are 390 px wide, a 195 px effective viewport, so they show the narrowest layout. A message that needs the wide zoomed form asks for a 1440 frame at 200% (720 px effective).

B10. Greyscale. Each light 03 artboard repeats the light grid at 50% scale, fully desaturated, unless the message sets a different scope. Next to each cell, print "Reads without colour: yes — <cue>", or the failure and its fix where the message names one.

B11. Increase Contrast. Each light 03 artboard shows what changes, or prints "Increase Contrast: nothing changes — <why>". By default, text.secondary becomes text.strong (dark: dark text.strong). Disabled text.muted stays, because the reason caption carries the meaning. Each message states its result.

B12. Grids, keys and cell labels. Rows are the message's variants and columns are its states, in the given order. Draw every cell. Under each row and column label, print "key: <key>" in caption 12/16 text.secondary. Keys are lowercase and hyphenated, with no "/", spaces, fixture strings or dates. Labels may be longer and may quote fixtures. Each message lists its keys, and cell labels and publish names use only those keys. A cell that "does not apply" is an empty surface.base card reading "Does not apply — <reason>" in caption 12/16 text.secondary; a shared reason is printed in each cell. Never leave a cell blank or skip a row or column.

B13. Targets. The minimum hit area is 44pt on iOS, 48dp with 8dp gaps on Android, and 44px on web: "target (B13)". Draw it as a 1 px dashed text.secondary outline labelled "target 44pt / 48dp / 44px". Point a small "not a target" label at any mark or glyph inside a row.

B14. Focus vs selection. Focus is a 2 px border.focus ring (dark: dark border.focus) with a 2 px gap outside the shape. Selection is a fill plus a glyph, plus the edge or ink change the message states. Never show selection with a ring alone, or focus with a fill.

B15. Motion. Nothing animates unless a message says so. Where motion exists, draw its Reduce Motion pose and its end pose beside it. Any exemption from the house style's 300ms limit is stated in the message and recorded on Notes.

B16. Fixtures and dates. Use only the house-style FIXTURES and the strings quoted in the messages. TODAY is Mon 19 Oct 2026, 6:10 PM Pacific. Compute every relative time from it: "observed 7:00 AM" is "11 hours ago", Mon 26 Oct is "in 7 days", and Sat 10 Oct is "9 days ago". Date rows put the relative count first ("in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct"). "Tonight", "Today" and "Tomorrow" stand alone, with no date. A time today shows no weekday ("As of 7:40 AM"). Any other string goes on Notes, section B.

B17. Air readings. The AQI track belongs to AqiBand, which is not on this board. Air rows show the value line and caption only. No EPA ColorVision Assist hue appears, and no text sits on an AQI fill.

======================================================================
00a · NOTES (one artboard, built up across the project)
======================================================================
ProvenanceMark's last part creates 00a · Notes, and each later component's last batch updates it. On each update, redraw the whole artboard, keep every earlier entry word for word, and add the new entries under the component's subheading. Print numbered lists in body 16/24 text.primary on surface.base, in five sections:
  A. Deviations and decisions (each needs a founder yes or no).
  B. Invented strings.
  C. Omitted or merged states ("none" if every cell was drawn).
  D. Open questions (only where two readings would give materially different components).
  E. Publish index (every PUBLISH name, one per line, grouped by component).

  00.A10 The dark text.strong, text.muted, border.strong and surface.muted values come from the published design system, not the house style. Dark text.strong is intentionally brighter than dark text.primary, for Increase Contrast.
  00.A11 Artboards are 1440 px wide unless a component message sets a wider grid artboard; each such width is recorded under that component.
  00.A12 Publish-name size and platform slot casing: size codes uppercase (XS, S, M, L, OG), platform codes lowercase (ios, android, web), otherwise "any".
  00.B1 Board annotations: "Does not apply — …" reasons, "not a target", "target 44pt / 48dp / 44px", "Reads without colour: yes — …", "Increase Contrast: nothing changes — …".

PURPOSE (print): The only way the product says how sure it is about a fact: three shapes, one meaning each, used everywhere.
USED IN (print): x-provenance-sheet, x-date-sheet, x-place-file, f5-today-calendar-strip, f4-today-pickup-card, f7-today-widget, f7-widget-gallery, f7-widget-howto-sheet, f7-widget-tap-landing, f1-today-tab, f3-household-calendar, f3-household-notifications, f8-scale-strips, f8-compare-arrival-header, f8-compare-reveal, f8-compare-sheet, f8-og-compare-card, f8-seasonal-aha, f6-place-section-details, f10-extraction-confirm, f10-bill-provenance, f10-bill-trend, f10-mail-day-triage, f11-keeper-strip, f1-claim-receipt.

ANATOMY (on 01-anatomy: each silhouette at L 56pt with callouts, then all sizes in a row)
- OFFICIAL: a solid disc. The diameter equals the size.
- UNCONFIRMED: a ring with the same outer diameter and a transparent centre. Stroke width: XS 12 → 1.5px, S 16 → 2px, M 24 → 3px, L 56 → 7px. Never thinner than 1.5px.
- YOU ADDED: a solid disc with a tick KNOCKED OUT of it. The tick is a true cut-out that shows the surface behind, not a second colour painted on top. The tick spans the middle 56% of the diameter. Its stroke width equals the ring stroke for that size (XS 1.5, S 2, M 3, L 7), with round caps and joins. This drawing survives one-colour tinting.
- Ink: text.secondary (4.83:1 on base) or darker in light mode; dark text.secondary in dark mode. Add a crossed-out swatch row labelled "never border.* · never text.muted" (border.default is 1.24:1, text.muted is 2.54:1).
- Sizes, each with its use printed:
  XS 12pt / 12dp / 12px: the smallest size at which the three shapes can still be told apart (strip cells, widget, tray previews).
  S 16pt: list rows and captions.
  M 24pt: the sheet legend.
  L 56pt: the provenance sheet header.
  OG 28px at 1200 wide: the share-card minimum.
- Below 12pt, no mark is drawn. Show a row labelled "10pt → no mark" that prints the words instead: "Pickup day · Thursday · On record, not confirmed".
- Spacing: 8pt (spacing.2) between the mark and its text, shown with a dimension line.
- LEGEND specimen (at M 24pt, stacked): [drawn official mark] "Official" · [drawn unconfirmed mark] "On record, not confirmed" · [drawn you-added mark] "You added this". Where a legend is written "● Official · ○ … · ✓ …", those characters stand for the drawn marks: always render the vector mark, never a font character.

text.secondary #6B7280 4.83:1 on base · dark text.secondary #94A3B8 6.96:1 on dark base, 5.71:1 on dark raised · stale: text.primary #111827 at 50% (the B7 50% figures) · dark stale: dark text.primary #E5E7EB at 50% (B7) · tinted widget: primary.700 #0369a1 on surface.base 5.93:1 (light) and primary.500 #0ea5e9 on dark surface.raised 5.28:1 (dark), never dimmed (at 50% they drop to 2.24:1 and 2.36:1) · never: primary.500 on surface.base 2.77:1, border.default 1.24:1, text.muted 2.54:1, text.secondary at 50% 1.98:1.

VARIANT × STATE GRID (02-variants-states: 6 rows × 5 columns; each cell is a 358-wide row at S 16pt on surface.base unless a column rule says otherwise)
Columns (label → key): default → default · stale (dimmed + age words) → stale · inside tap target → in-target · tinted/accented widget rendering (silhouette only) → tinted-widget · greyscale → greyscale.
Rows (label → key), used in every column unless a column rule says otherwise:
 R1 official (filled) → official: "Flood zone" / "Zone X — minimal flood hazard", caption "FEMA · area zone · effective Sep 2021".
 R2 unconfirmed (hollow) → unconfirmed: "Pickup day" / "Thursday", caption "City of Camas · city pickup schedule · as of Sat 10 Oct" (Place B).

 R4 read-from-your-photo → read-from-photo: a machine read before the user commits it, drawn with the UNCONFIRMED ring. Row "Clark Public Utilities" / "$142.18 · due in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct". Under the uncertain value only (the due date), add the flag line "We weren't sure — check this" in caption 12/16 text.strong with a 12pt text.strong pencil glyph (not a circle). Beside the cell, draw a small arrow to a copy of the row after commit, where the mark becomes YOU ADDED, labelled "on commit → you-added".

Column rules:
 - default: as above.
 - stale: dim the mark to text.primary at 50% and replace the caption with that row's own stale caption. The dimming is never the only cue: the age words always appear. Per row:
   R1: Does not apply — an effective date does not age.
   R2: dimmed ring, caption "City of Camas · city pickup schedule · as of Sat 10 Oct — 9 days ago".
   R3: Does not apply — your own entry does not age.
   R4: Does not apply — a pre-commit read is not refreshed.
   R5: print "same as stale variant" (R5 is already stale) and draw the R5 row.

 - tinted-widget: draw the row at XS 12pt inside a 158×158 widget crop rendered in one accent hue. - Web 200% zoom (390): the same, with the SVG sized in em.

- GREYSCALE (this component overrides B10): do not redraw the grid. Print "Greyscale: see the greyscale column on 02-variants-states — every cell reads yes — shape". Draw one deliberate FAIL example labelled "WRONG": two discs that differ only in hue, with the fix label "fix: shape, not colour".

Dark twin (03 · dark): the AX5 and 200% frames in dark tokens, the XS strip, and the three marks in dark text.strong labelled "Increase Contrast ink". It leaves out the web zoom frame and the greyscale pointer, because greyscale does not depend on theme.

INSTEAD OF (print on 01-anatomy · light)
- Instead of filled vs hollow for any other meaning (sender vs you in compare, taken vs open founding slots, density), draw labelled pointers, or solid vs hatched segments plus a numeral — because filled vs hollow means provenance and nothing else.
- Instead of a confidence percentage, bar or star, draw one of the three marks plus its word — because the product never grades certainty.
- Instead of a hollow mark on an official public dataset (EPA radon zone, USFS wildfire hazard), draw the filled mark and put the limit in the caption's scope word ("county-wide estimate") — because hollow means "not confirmed", not "coarse".
- Instead of a tick painted in a second colour on top of the disc, knock the tick out — because a second colour disappears under one-colour widget tinting.
- Instead of a light tinted widget in primary.500, use primary.700 on surface.base — because primary.500 is 2.77:1 on white and marks need 3:1.
- Instead of dimming a tinted widget mark for stale, keep the full tint and add the age words — because a dimmed tint drops below 3:1.
- Instead of making an 8px dot the tap target, make the enclosing row or cell the target — because a small mark cannot be hit reliably.
- Instead of a bare "Unverified" suffix on every row, show the word once per surface in a legend — because repetition is noise and "unverified" is forbidden.
- Instead of text.secondary at 50% for stale, use text.primary at 50% — because the first drops to 1.98:1.
- Instead of one age suffix on every row, give each fact its own stale caption — because an effective date or your own entry does not age.

<size|platform> is the size the cell is drawn at (XS, S, M, L, OG); tinted-widget cells are XS. Examples: "ProvenanceMark / official / default / S / light" · "ProvenanceMark / you-added / tinted-widget / XS / dark".

LINK RULE (applies to every cell, crop and frame)
A caption is a link only when its source has a URL. A link caption shows all three of these: the authority word in primary.700 (dark: primary.400 (dark link)) with an underline; the trailing external-link glyph in the same colour; and the dashed target (B13) around the caption line. A caption with no URL is all text.secondary (text.strong on sunken), with no underline, no glyph and no target.

- Ink: text.secondary on base, raised or app surfaces; text.strong on sunken. Draw two copies side by side, one on base and one on sunken, each labelled with its tokens and ratios.

INSTEAD OF (print on 01-anatomy)
- Instead of hiding the source behind a tooltip or "learn more", print authority · scope · as-of on the value — because almost nobody opens the sheet.
- Instead of labelling a frozen reading "today", write "on Sat 12 Sep 2026" — because a shared card is read days later.
- Instead of making a caption with no URL tappable, draw it flat — because a target that goes nowhere breaks trust.
- Instead of "Sources:" on wide layouts, give every row its own caption — because the collapsed line exists only for 320–360 widths (except the OG image).
- Instead of cutting a long authority short with an ellipsis, wrap to a second line — because the authority is the caveat.
- Instead of a hollow mark on a county-wide official estimate, use the filled mark and the scope word — because hollow means "not confirmed".

ANATOMY (on 01-anatomy: callouts on a 358-wide card header, "1107 NE Birchfield Ct" with the "Saved place · Only you" ScopeChip, and the line under it)
- ① Placement: directly under the location row or card header, 4pt / 4dp / 4px (spacing.1) below it.
- ② Caption 12/16/400 in text.secondary (text.strong on sunken).
- ③ Optional leading 16pt / 16dp / 16px glyph, in text.secondary with an 8 gap: offline (a cloud with a slash) or retry (a circular arrow drawn as an open arc with an arrowhead, not a closed ring).
- ④ Optional 2pt / 2dp / 2px indeterminate hairline under the header, full card width, in primary.700 (5.93:1 on base; at least 3:1 on its surface). It is each platform's own system indeterminate progress indicator (iOS linear ProgressView, Android Material 3 LinearProgressIndicator, web an indeterminate progress bar), tinted primary.700, with no custom duration or easing. It runs only if the refresh takes 1s or longer. This is the only motion on the board (the B15 exemption; see 04.A1). Draw three poses side by side:
   running: a short segment partway along the track, with the note "system indeterminate progress indicator · no custom duration · exempt from the 300ms rule, stopped within 5s (see Notes)".
   after 5s (the end pose): the hairline stops and is removed. "Updating…" stays in the line until the result arrives; then the line becomes "Updated just now" or the failed line (R3). Label it "idle loops stop within 5s".
   Reduce Motion: no hairline at all; the word "Updating…" carries the state.

Each variant exists in exactly one state (see 04.A6). Draw that one cell as described, and fill the row's other four cells with the reason given for that row (B12).

The refreshing, failed and offline cells: "Does not apply — this line appears only while fresh". The stale cell: "Does not apply — stale is stated per fact (R5)".

The other four cells: "Does not apply — this line appears only while one fact is stale".

ACCESSIBILITY (print on 01-anatomy)
- Changes are announced in a polite live region, never an assertive one (iOS: an accessibility announcement queued behind current speech (default or low priority); Android: accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"; web: aria-live="polite").
- Non-colour: stale is stated in words.
- Target rule: Retry is a target (B13).
- Ageing text is announced once, not every minute.
- Spoken example: "You're offline, as of 7:04 AM".

COPY (print on 01-anatomy)
- Relative time for recency ("Updated 12m ago"). "As of" plus an absolute time for offline or frozen data ("as of 7:04 AM"); add the weekday only when the time is not today.
- Never "Last synced", "refreshed at" or "last seen".
- Never a disappearing toast as the only proof.

PLATFORMS (print on 01-anatomy)
- iOS widgets use the system Text(date, style: .relative).
- Android widgets use the equivalent system relative-time text.
- The hairline is each platform's system indeterminate progress indicator.
- Web: a polite live region.

INSTEAD OF (print on 01-anatomy)
- Instead of dimming, skeletoning or reflowing a warm screen while refreshing, keep it and show "Updating…" (and the hairline after 1s) — because stale content is still useful.
- Instead of a hairline that loops until the request ends, stop it at 5s and leave "Updating…" — because idle loops stop within 5s.
- Instead of a custom animated hairline, use the platform's system indeterminate indicator — because a custom loop is a motion spec nobody needs to maintain.
- Instead of greying a whole widget when only AQI is old, put the age words on the air line — because the other facts are still current.
- Instead of a toast, use this line — because toasts vanish before people read them.
- Instead of "Last synced", write "Updated" or "As of" — because "synced" is jargon.

PUBLISH KEYS
Variants: updating · updated · failed · offline · fact-stale · widget-horizon. States: fresh · refreshing · stale · failed · offline. <size|platform> is "any". Example: "FreshnessLine / updating / refreshing / any / light".

- Exactly one chip per row. Sentence case. Dates show the weekday.

INSTEAD OF (print)
- Warning-hue text on a warning tint → text.strong on surface.sunken with the hue on the glyph only, because warning text on its tint is about 3:1.
- Two chips on one row → the one status that matters, because two chips compete and get misread.
- A status chip on a person ("Verified", "Active") → the role in plain text, because people are not statuses.
- A warning-tinted countdown pill (founding window) → a neutral date chip, because countdowns pressure people.
- The date before the count ("Mon 26 Oct · in 7 days") → "in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct", because the house style and DateRow lead with the count and every consuming surface copies this chip.
- A disc-shaped status dot → the listed glyphs, because circles belong to ProvenanceMark.

TILE → GLYPH MAP (print)
Pickup day → 3 · Move-in date → 5 · Lease ends → 6 · Notice deadline → 7 · Insurance renews → 8 · Warranty ends → 9 · HOA dues → 10 · Property-tax appeal → 11 · Voter registration → 13 · Bill → 14.

ACCESSIBILITY (print)
- Decorative (hidden) when a text label is adjacent; otherwise labelled with the row label ("Recycling"). Always paired with visible text; widget and tray glyphs carry their word.
- Each tile is one element: "Pickup day, selected, 1 of 10" (iOS: a button with the selected trait; Android: RadioButton semantics; web: role="radio" inside role="radiogroup").
- Non-colour: shape plus label; selection is the dot or check plus the edge, fill and ink change.
- Target: the tile cell or row, never the glyph alone (B13).

COPY (print)
- Tile labels, exactly: Pickup day · Move-in date · Lease ends · Notice deadline · Insurance renews · Warranty ends · HOA dues · Property-tax appeal · Voter registration · Bill.
- Row labels, exactly: the "row label" column of THE SET. The ones with no tile are Garbage · Recycling · Recycling and garbage · Bulk pickup · Property-tax due · Home date · Task · Package.
- "Pickup day", never "trash day", "garbage day" or "bin day"; "Date", never "event" or "deadline item".

PLATFORMS (print)
- The same glyph on all three platforms. The widget glyph is silhouette-safe like ProvenanceMark: one ink, inner detail cut out, so it survives one-colour accented rendering.
- The one-column large-text list: a trailing check on iOS and web; Material 3 radio buttons on Android.

INSTEAD OF (print)
- Hue-coded glyphs as the only class cue → a silhouette per kind plus a label, because hue alone fails in greyscale and for colour-blind users.
- An unlabelled glyph → the kind's row label beside it, because the glyphs are not universal.
- Guessing a tile's glyph → the TILE → GLYPH map, because every later picker copies this one.
- Selection shown with the focus ring → fill + edge + radio dot + label ink, because selection must look different from focus.
- An empty-ring radio on iOS or web large-text rows → a trailing check on the selected row and nothing on the others, because iOS has no radio control and an empty ring is the unconfirmed mark's shape.
- Emoji or a second icon set → the Pantopus icon style, because the house style forbids a new icon set.

SetupWebiOSAndroid0 artboards2,808 words

Board rules for every component on this board. Send first; draws nothing.

Use the Pantopus house style pasted above. This project is Foundations board 00b: Data instruments. This message sets up the board. Don't draw anything yet.

WHAT THIS BOARD IS FOR
This project draws seven components as reference specimens, not as screens: ScaleStrip, AqiBand, FourteenDayStrip, YearBand, SlotMeter, PublicPointMap and FactCount. Later screen prompts, sent from separate projects that can't see this one, ask for these components by exact name. Once published, these specimens are the only definition of each component. Draw every number, token and string exactly as the component messages give it.

HOW THIS PROJECT RUNS
- This message holds the board rules: G1–G8 and R1–R12. They apply to every artboard in this project. Later messages call them "the board rules from the setup message".
- After this message, I'll send one component message per turn, in this order: ScaleStrip, AqiBand, FourteenDayStrip, YearBand, SlotMeter, PublicPointMap, FactCount.
- ScaleStrip and AqiBand each arrive in two parts (part 1, then part 2). The two parts count as one component message. Part 2 relies on everything in part 1.
- Each component message (or part) includes its ARTBOARDS list and a BATCH PLAN. Draw only the first batch. Then stop and wait until I type "continue" or send the next part. Never start another component's artboards early.
- The last batch of every component updates 00b · Notes (R12).
- Everything you need is in the house style, this message, and the current and earlier component messages in this project. Don't open other projects.

PUBLISH (my step, after I accept a component)
When I accept a component, I add it to the Pantopus design system under its exact name. That includes its light and dark specimens and every variant and state. Your job is to make that step mechanical:
- Give every drawn grid cell and every named extra specimen a publish name (R10).
- List the names on 00b · Notes.
- Stand-ins (R11) and anything marked "do not publish" never get a publish name.

SHARED GRAMMAR (all seven instruments)
G1. Each instrument states its fact in words and numbers. The graphic repeats the fact and never replaces it.
G2. Nothing adds up to a grade, score, percentage or verdict. No progress ring, completion ring, countdown, streak or confetti appears anywhere. An authority's own band names are allowed even when they contain a percentage; each component message lists the allowed ones. "N of M" appears only where a component message allows it.
G3. Nothing depends on colour alone. The EPA AQI hues are the only sanctioned colour scale, and even there the category is printed in words.
G4. Three shapes mean provenance (00a · ProvenanceMark) and nothing else: a solid disc (Official), a ring (On record, not confirmed) and a solid disc with a knocked-out tick (You added this). No position marker, pointer, bullet, callout end, segment or badge on this board is a plain disc or ring. A component message that needs an exception describes it.
G5. A mark, cell or segment is never a tap target on its own. The target is the row, the whole instrument or a labelled button.
G6. Each instrument has a one-sentence summary and a spoken label, and both are printed on its artboards. The same facts also appear nearby as rows or a list.
G7. Every provenance mark keeps at least 3:1 contrast in every state. Staleness is always stated in words.
G8. Widgets and the share card are standalone surfaces. They print the provenance word next to each mark or in a legend line inside the block.

BOARD RULES
R1 · Artboard format and naming.
- Name every artboard "00b · <Component> · <NN-name> · <light|dark>", exactly as the component's ARTBOARDS list gives it. This overrides the house-style artboard pattern, because one specimen artboard shows several platforms. The last artboard is "00b · Notes".
- Each artboard is 1440 wide and as tall as its content. Light artboards use surface.app; dark artboards use dark surface.app.
- Above each artboard, print its exact name in label 13/18/600 text.strong.
- At the top inside each artboard, print three lines, as the component message gives them:
  - the component name, in h1 30/36/700 text.primary
  - its purpose line, in body 16/24 text.secondary
  - "Used in: <surface ids>", in caption 12/16 text.secondary
- Section headings use overline 11/16/600 caps, for example ANATOMY, VARIANT × STATE, AX5 AND 200%, GREYSCALE, IN CONTEXT, ACCESSIBILITY and INSTEAD OF.

R2 · Frames and cards.
- Draw specimens at true size (1pt = 1px on the artboard) inside plain frames, named as the message names them: iOS 393, Android 412, web-390, web-1440, and the widget outlines 338×158 and 338×354.
- In the three phone frames, draw the specimen card 358 wide with 16pt padding, which leaves 326pt of content width. Left-align the card at a 16pt frame margin. The right margin is then 19pt in iOS 393, 16pt in web-390 and 38pt in Android 412.
- All phone geometry assumes 326pt of content width unless a message says otherwise.
- Light cards use surface.base, radius lg 12, shadow sm and 16pt padding.
- Dark cards use dark surface.raised with a 1px dark border.strong decorative edge. The card edge carries no meaning, so the 3:1 minimum doesn't apply to it.
- Each component message gives its own web-1440 card width.

R3 · Units.
- A size given in pt is the same number in dp (Android) and px (web).
- Only target minimums differ by platform: 44pt on iOS, 48dp with 8dp gaps on Android, and 44px on web.
- Spacing uses the 4px scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64.
- A few micro offsets inside instruments are deliberately off that scale: 6, 3, 2 and 1pt. Use them only where a component message states them, and never for layout spacing.
- Type uses only these sizes:
  - the house type scale
  - medium (500) weights of body, bodySmall and caption at the same sizes: bodyMedium, bodySmallMedium and captionMedium
  - the R7 sizes
  - the 11pt widget minimum
  - OG sizes, where a component message states them

R4 · Callouts.
- Callouts sit in an annotation gutter outside the UI, in caption 12/16 text.strong. Gutter labels ("specimen", "specimen value", "stand-in — …") use the same style.
- Leader lines are 1px text.secondary and end in a short perpendicular tick, never a dot (G4).
- Dimension lines are 1px text.secondary with 4pt end ticks.
- Each callout names the part, its size and its token, for example "Track · 12pt · fill surface.raised · keyline 1px text.secondary".
- Callouts appear on 01-anatomy artboards and wherever a message asks for them.

R5 · Tokens and dark mode.
- Label every colour by its token name. Hex values appear on the board only in contrast tables a message asks for and in the AQI swatch row.
- The dark hex values in these rules and in the component messages are for drawing. In callouts, print the token name followed by "(dark)", for example "surface.raised (dark)".
- On dark artboards, use exactly this mapping:
  - surfaces: surface.base → #0F172A · surface.raised → #1E293B · surface.app → #020617 · surface.sunken → #0F172A · surface.muted → #111827
  - text: text.primary → #E5E7EB · text.secondary → #94A3B8 · text.strong → #F1F5F9
  - borders: border.default → #1F2937 and border.strong → #374151 (both are decoration only) · border.focus → #38BDF8
  - primary.700 → #38BDF8. This applies to links, text buttons and any edge a message names, because primary.700 is only 2.47:1 on dark raised.
- These tokens keep their light values in dark mode and are labelled by token name:
  - the primary.600 fill (3.57:1 on dark raised)
  - semantic.error glyphs (3.03:1)
  - semantic.warning glyphs (4.59:1)
- Semantic hues go on glyphs only.
- On dark cards, surface.sunken fills (#0F172A on #1E293B) look darker than the card. This is intended, because keylines and text carry the edges.
- A sunken-filled shape that sits directly on dark base uses dark surface.raised instead, so that it stays visible.
- Never use the light infoBg wash in dark mode, because dark text.primary on it is only 1.16:1. Component messages give the dark highlight.
- The EPA AQI hues never change in dark mode.
- This board draws no selection state.

R6 · Contrast numbers (WCAG 2). Opacities are alpha-blended over their surface first. Use these numbers and don't recompute them. Print only the rows a message asks for. A "tinted cell" is surface.sunken at 40% over base.
Light:
- text.secondary: 4.83 on base · 4.63 on raised · 4.51 on app · 4.39 on sunken. That is below 4.5, so text on sunken uses text.strong.
- text.strong: 9.37 on sunken · 10.31 on base
- text.primary: 17.74 on base · 16.12 on sunken
- primary.700: 5.93 on base · 5.68 on raised · 5.39 on sunken
- primary.600 fill: 4.10 on base
- glyphs: semantic.error 4.83 on base · semantic.warning 3.19 on base
- stale mark (the 00a stale variant, text.primary at 50%): 3.39 on base · 3.36 on raised · 3.34 on app · 3.32 on sunken
- on a tinted cell: text.secondary 4.65 · stale mark 3.36
- Never use text.secondary at 50% or text.muted for readable text. Both fail 4.5:1.
Dark:
- text.secondary: 6.96 on dark base · 5.71 on dark raised
- text.primary: 11.82 on dark raised · 14.42 on dark base
- text.strong: 16.30 on dark base · 13.35 on dark raised
- #38BDF8: 6.83 on dark raised · 8.33 on dark base
- stale mark (dark text.primary at 50%): 4.45 on dark base · 4.10 on dark raised · 4.48 on dark app
- on a dark tinted cell: text.secondary 6.23 · stale mark 4.27
- decoration only: dark border.strong 1.42 on dark raised · dark border.default 1.00 on dark raised

R7 · AX5 and 200%.
- iOS AX5 sizes: h1 58 · h2 56 · h3 55 · body and bodyMedium 53 · bodySmall and bodySmallMedium 49 · label 44 · caption and captionMedium 43 · overline 40.
- Android 200% sizes (Android 14 non-linear scaling): h1 38 · h2 36 · h3 34 · body 28 · bodySmall 26 · label 25 · caption 24 · overline 22. Medium weights use the same sizes as their base styles.
- Web: 200% browser zoom on web-1440, which gives an effective layout 720 CSS px wide.
- Graphic geometry keeps its size, and text reflows around it. This covers tracks, cells, segments, markers, glyph-only buttons, and marks inside cells, lanes and tracks.
- Marks inside text lines (captions, rows, legends) scale with their text.
- Text wraps and never truncates or ends in an ellipsis. Side-by-side pairs stack. Widgets fall back to text only, as each message states.
- Draw iOS AX5 in a 393 frame and Android 200% in a 412 frame, each as tall as needed.

R8 · Greyscale.
- Redraw the listed specimens at 100% desaturation.
- Under each one, print in caption text.secondary the non-colour cue that still carries the meaning, in the words the component message gives.

R9 · Grids and keys.
- A variant × state grid has variant rows and state columns, in the order the message gives.
- Print each row and column label in label 13/18/600 text.strong. Under each label, print its key as "key: <key>" in caption 12/16 text.secondary.
- A key is lowercase and hyphenated. It never contains spaces, "/", a fixture string or a date. Each component message lists its keys; use them exactly.
- Each cell holds one specimen at true size, or the stacked specimens the message asks for. Under the specimen, print the cell's keys, for example "detail · stale".
- A combination that has no meaning prints "n/a — <reason>" in caption text.secondary and nothing else. Use the one reason the message gives. Never leave a cell blank.

R10 · Publish names. Give one name to each drawn grid cell and each extra specimen, in one of two forms:
- "<Component> / <variant key> / <state key> / <light|dark>"
- "<Component> / extra / <extra key> / <light|dark>"
Names use keys only. n/a cells get no name.

R11 · Borrowed parts and stand-ins.

The stand-ins:
- 00a · ProvenanceMark: a mark at XS 12pt or S 16pt, in text.secondary at full opacity.
  - Official: a solid disc.
  - On record, not confirmed: a ring with a stroke of at least 1.5px.
  - You added this: a solid disc with a knocked-out tick (a true cut-out).
  - Stale variant: the same shape in text.primary at 50%, always paired with age words.
- 00a · SourceCaption: one caption 12/16 line in text.secondary (text.strong on sunken), in the pattern [ProvenanceMark S] authority · scope word · as-of. It wraps and never truncates.
- 00a · FreshnessLine: one caption line in text.secondary that states the age in words, with an optional 16pt leading glyph.
- 00a · ScopeChip: a 24pt pill on surface.sunken, holding a 12pt person or house glyph and the label in label 13/18 text.strong.
- 00a · KindGlyph: a 24pt line icon with a 2pt stroke, in text.strong.
- 00c · InlineErrorRow: a row in the component's own slot, with no tinted background. It holds:

- 00c · DateRow: a row at least 56pt tall. It holds:

- 00c · FactRow: a 56pt row. It holds the label in bodySmall text.secondary above the value in body text.primary, a ProvenanceMark and a trailing chevron.
- 00c · TextActionRow (outbound): a row at least 44pt tall with a 1px text.secondary edge, a verb-led label in primary.700 and a trailing "↗".
- 00d · WarmingSkeleton: surface.sunken shapes with the component's final geometry and radius, and no text.
  - It reserves the exact final height.
  - It shimmers by default and is static under Reduce Motion.
- 00d · QuietDayReceipt: draw only the form a component message describes, exactly as described.

Part 1 holds the full specification and the first four artboards. Part 2, my next message, adds artboards 05–08, the dark twins and the Notes, and relies on everything in this part.

ARTBOARDS AND BATCH PLAN FOR PART 1
Draw these four, using the exact names and this order. Then stop and wait for part 2.

PURPOSE (print it): The four-layer reading instrument. It draws one row per authority on that authority's own ordered bands, and it never adds up to a grade.
USED IN (print it): f8-scale-strips, f6-place-section-details, f8-compare-arrival-header, f8-compare-reveal, f8-compare-sheet, f8-og-compare-card.
WEB-1440 CARD: 640px wide, with 608px of content.
SPECIMEN CLOCKS
- Ready Air rows, including the compare "You" row, are drawn at 7:10 AM on Mon 19 Oct, so "observed 7:00 AM" counts as fresh. Print "specimen time 7:10 AM" in the gutter.
- Stale Air rows use TODAY, 6:10 PM.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy; put a callout on every part)
- Row order is fixed as Flood · Wildfire · Air · Radon, and rows are never re-sorted, because people compare rows by position.
- A row contains, from top to bottom:
  - the layer name, in label 13/18/600 text.strong
  - the value line "Word · number", in bodyMedium 16/24/500 text.primary
  - the track zone
  - the band names
  - 00a · SourceCaption
- Row padding is 12pt top and bottom. Gaps: name → value 4pt · value → track zone 8pt · track zone → band names 4pt · band names → caption 8pt.
- Each row is at least 48pt tall and is a single target. Markers and pointers are never targets.
- Layout:
  - Below 560pt (phones and web-390), the row is stacked, with a 326pt track.
  - At 560pt and wider (web-1440), the row has two columns: left 237px, gap 16px, right 355px. The left column stacks the name, the value line and the SourceCaption. The right column holds the track zone and the band names, top-aligned with the value line.
  - AX5 and 200% are stacked.
  - Part 2 defines the OG column.
- Track zone: 24pt tall, with a 12pt track centred in it.
- Track:
  - equal-width bands per layer (the layers don't share an axis)
  - filled surface.raised
  - 1.5px text.secondary separators (4.63:1 on raised)
  - a 1px text.secondary keyline with radius xs 4 around the whole track
  - the least hazard on the left
- Occupied band: a 2px text.primary outline inside its edges.
- Marker: a vertical capsule, 4 × 20pt, radius pill.
  - Core: text.primary. Halo: 2px surface.base, which makes it 8 × 24pt overall. The halo is #0F172A in dark.
  - It is centred in the occupied band and extends 4pt beyond the track top and bottom.
  - It is never a disc (G4).
- Band names, in caption 12/16 text.secondary:
  - Up to 2 lines each, never truncated.
  - Flood and Radon print all their names. Wildfire prints the two end names plus the occupied one.
  - The occupied name is set in captionMedium 12/16/500 text.primary, directly under the marker. If it comes within 8pt of an end name, it replaces that end name.
  - Air prints "0–50" · "51–100" · "101–150" · "151–200" · "201–300" · "301+", with the occupied range in captionMedium text.primary.
- Bands:
  - Flood, by annual chance: "Minimal (X)" · "0.2% a year (shaded X)" · "1% a year or more (A/V zones)". The value line prints the actual zone code. These FEMA annual-chance names and "1% chance each year" are the band names G2 allows.
  - Wildfire (USFS): "Very low" · "Low" · "Moderate" · "High" · "Very high".
  - Radon: "Zone 3 · low potential" · "Zone 2 · moderate potential" · "Zone 1 · highest potential". Never "N of M".
  - Air: the AqiBand instrument-row variant. It is the only coloured track. The next component defines AqiBand; draw this row exactly as follows:
    - six equal-width 12pt segments in the house-style EPA ColorVision Assist hues
    - 2px gaps in the host surface
    - a 1px text.secondary keyline on each segment, with radius xs 4 on the outer corners
    - on the occupied segment, a 2px text.primary inner outline
    - the same 4 × 20pt capsule, placed by value within its segment
    - no reading: segments in surface.sunken with their keylines, and no marker
    - the value line leaves out the pollutant
- Fixture rows (HOME A). All are Official; "●" stands for the drawn Official mark.

  | Row | Label | Value | Occupied | Caption |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Flood | "Flood zone" | "Zone X — minimal flood hazard" | band 1 | "● FEMA · area zone · effective Sep 2021" |
  | Wildfire | "Wildfire hazard potential" | "Moderate · 3 of 5" | band 3 | "● USFS · quarter-mile area · 2023" |
  | Air | "Air quality index (AQI)" | "AQI 42 · Good" | 84% of Good | "● AirNow · nearest monitors · observed 7:00 AM" |
  | Radon | "Radon zone" | "Zone 1 — highest potential (county)" | band 3 | "● EPA · county-wide estimate — only a test tells you about this home" |

- Summary. Print this one sentence under the 01 fixture instrument: "Flood Zone X, minimal flood hazard; Wildfire Moderate, 3 of 5; Air AQI 42, Good; Radon Zone 1, county-wide."
- Specimen value: a Flood row with "Zone AE — 1% chance each year (about 1 in 4 over 30 years)" and band 3 occupied.

VARIANTS [row keys]
- V1 Flood [flood] · V2 Wildfire [wildfire] · V3 Radon [radon] · V4 Air [air].
- V5 compare [compare]: two identical labelled pointers replace the capsule. Filled vs hollow means provenance only.
  - Track zone, 60pt tall, from top to bottom:
    - a 16pt line "Dana", in captionMedium text.primary
    - the 8pt sender pointer
    - the 12pt track
    - the 8pt "You" pointer
    - a 16pt line "You"
    Band names sit 4pt below the track zone.
  - Pointers: triangles 12 wide × 8 tall, in text.primary with a 2px surface.base halo.
    - The sender pointer points down, with its tip on the track top. The "You" pointer points up, with its tip on the track bottom.
    - Each pointer is centred in its band. On Air, it is placed by value.
  - Each occupied band is outlined; a band both places share gets one outline. The two pointers share an x position on the non-Air layers, and on Air only when the values are equal.
  - Value lines: "Dana: <value>" and "You: <value>". When the band is shared, print one line, "Both: <value>".
  - Chip: "Same band" or "Different band", right-aligned on the layer-name line.
    - A 24pt pill in surface.sunken, 8pt side padding, captionMedium text.strong, no glyph and no hue.
    - On compare rows, the layer-name line is 24pt tall, and the name is vertically centred on the chip. The other row gaps are unchanged.
  - Header: "Dana · Camas, WA — what's on record for this area".
- V6 no data [no-data] (Flood, Wildfire, Radon): bands in surface.sunken, keyline and separators unchanged, no marker and no outline, value "Not on record".
- V7 not studied (Flood): the same greyed track, with the value "FEMA hasn't mapped flood hazard here".
- V8 non-burnable (Wildfire): the same greyed track, with the value "Non-burnable land cover (USFS)".
- V6–V8 must each look different from Wildfire "Very low", because missing data is not a low reading.
- V9 frozen [frozen]:
  - Captions end "as of Sat 12 Sep 2026".
  - The Air caption reads "AirNow · on Sat 12 Sep 2026", and the Air value reads "AQI 42 · Good · on Sat 12 Sep".
- V10 collapsed [collapsed], for arrival headers below 640px:
  - one wrapping body row, at least 44pt tall
  - the whole row is the target, and there are no tracks
  - text: "Dana · Camas, WA · Flood X · Wildfire Moderate · Air 42 · Radon Zone 1 ›"

STATES [column keys]
- loading [loading]: 00d · WarmingSkeleton.
  - Only the track keyline and separators show.
  - The label and value become surface.sunken bars of 60×12 and 140×16.
  - The exact row height is reserved.
- ready [ready].
- partial, loading [partial-loading]: some rows are ready and others are loading.
- partial, failed [partial-failed]: the Air row's slot shows 00c · InlineErrorRow "We couldn't reach AirNow just now" with Retry. The other rows are ready.
- differs [differs]: the "Different band" chip (V5).
- stale [stale], at 6:10 PM:
  - The Air row keeps its value and marker.
  - Its caption reads "AirNow · nearest monitors · observed 7:00 AM — 11 hours ago", with the 00a stale mark. The age words carry the staleness.
  - The other rows are unchanged.
- AX5 [ax5]: text stacked above a full-width track. Part 2 draws this, on 06.

DEVIATIONS FROM THE CONTRACT (part 2 records these on Notes D for my sign-off)
- The 4 × 20pt two-tone capsule replaces the contract's "Marker: 12pt two-tone".
- The 12 × 8 triangle pointers in V5 replace the contract's "same marker form" for compare.

PURPOSE (print it): The one officially coloured scale. It shows the EPA AQI with its category name and is drawn the same way everywhere air appears.
USED IN (print it): f1-today-air-band, f8-scale-strips, f6-place-section-details, f7-today-widget, f7-widget-gallery, f7-widget-howto-sheet, f7-widget-tap-landing, x-provenance-sheet, f8-og-compare-card, f8-compare-reveal.
WEB-1440 CARD: 640px wide, with 608px of content.

SPECIMEN CLOCKS
AirNow readings are hourly, so the age of a reading decides its state. On every artboard that shows one of these specimens, print its specimen time once in the gutter.
- Ready and offline specimens: 7:10 AM on Mon 19 Oct, so "observed 7:00 AM" counts as fresh.
- Alert and still-above specimens: 4:10 PM.
- Stale specimens: TODAY, 6:10 PM, which gives "— 11 hours ago".

ANATOMY (01-anatomy; put a callout on every part)
- Segments: six equal-width category segments in the EPA ColorVision Assist hues. These are the only non-token colours in the product.
- Swatch row: show the hues as a row, with each name and RGB value:
  - aqi.good: Good 158,255,145
  - aqi.moderate: Moderate 255,201,5
  - aqi.usg: Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups 255,130,5
  - aqi.unhealthy: Unhealthy 240,34,0
  - aqi.veryUnhealthy: Very Unhealthy 137,9,151
  - aqi.hazardous: Hazardous 100,0,21
- Segment height: 16pt in the detail variant (Today), 12pt in the instrument row, and 8pt in the widget micro variant.
- Gaps: 2px between segments, in the host surface. That is surface.base on light cards and surface.raised (dark) on dark cards.
- Keylines: each segment gets its own 1px text.secondary keyline, because some hues nearly vanish against their surface (Good is 1.22:1 and Moderate 1.54:1 on white; Hazardous is 1.08:1 on dark raised). The outer corners of the first and last segments have radius xs 4.
- Detail segment width: (326 − 5 × 2) ÷ 6 = 52.7pt. On web-1440: (608 − 10) ÷ 6 = 99.7px.
- Range labels: centred under each segment, in caption 12/16 text.secondary: "0–50" · "51–100" · "101–150" · "151–200" · "201–300" · "301+".
  - The occupied label switches to captionMedium text.primary.
  - The occupied segment gets a 2px text.primary inner outline.
- Marker: the ScaleStrip capsule, 4pt wide.
  - Core: text.primary. Halo: 2px surface.base. In dark mode the halo stays the fixed dark tone #0F172A.
  - Height is the segment height + 8pt: 24pt in detail, 20pt in the instrument row, 16pt in widget micro.
  - It is never a disc (G4).
  - It passes 3:1 on every hue in both themes, because one of its two tones always contrasts.
- Marker position:
  - Position within the segment = (value − segment low) ÷ (segment high − segment low).
  - For position only, the "301+" segment spans 301–500.
  - AQI 42 sits at 84% of Good. AQI 118 sits at 35% of Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.
  - Values above 500 clamp to the right end of "301+", and the actual number is still printed.
- Marker contrast table. Print it on 01: core and halo contrast against each hue.

  | Hue | Light core | Light halo | Dark core | Dark halo |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Good | 14.50 | 1.22 | 1.01 | 14.59 |
  | Moderate | 11.50 | 1.54 | 1.25 | 11.57 |
  | USG | 7.14 | 2.49 | 2.01 | 7.18 |
  | Unhealthy | 4.17 | 4.26 | 3.44 | 4.19 |
  | Very Unhealthy | 2.15 | 8.24 | 6.65 | 2.17 |
  | Hazardous | 1.31 | 13.52 | 10.92 | 1.32 |

- Value line: above the band, in bodyMedium text.primary.
  - Fixture: "AQI 42 · Good · PM2.5". Alert: "AQI 118 · Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups · PM2.5".
  - The category and number always sit on the card in text.primary, never on a fill (text.primary on Hazardous is only 1.31:1).
  - The value line is the visible summary.
  - Inside ScaleStrip, the pollutant is left out.
- Health statement: below the band, in body 16/24 text.primary, verbatim from EPA.
  - Good: "Air quality is satisfactory, and air pollution poses little or no risk."
  - Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups: "Members of sensitive groups may experience health effects. The general public is less likely to be affected." Then add the PM2.5 line: "People with heart or lung disease, older adults, children, and people of lower socioeconomic status are the groups most at risk."
- PANTOPUS NOTE: Pantopus context, labelled as ours. It appears on the alert and still-above specimens only.
  - It is a separate block below the EPA statement. The EPA statement stays above it, unchanged.
  - The block holds the overline "PANTOPUS NOTE", then, in bodySmall text.primary, "Your alert level is 101. You can change it in Notifications."
  - On still-above, the block holds a second line directly below that one, also in bodySmall text.primary: "Still above your alert level (101) since 4:00 PM. No new alert until it drops below 101 and rises again."
- Threshold rule: drawn at the user's chosen threshold (101, 151 or 201), never hard-coded.
  - A 1.5px dashed vertical rule (3 on, 2 off) in text.primary, extending 6pt beyond the band top and bottom.
  - When the threshold equals a segment's low value, centre the rule in the 2px gap before that segment. 101 sits in the Moderate/USG gap; 151 sits in the USG/Unhealthy gap.
  - The threshold number sits above the rule, in caption text.primary ("101").
  - "Crossed 101 at 4:00 PM" appears in bodySmallMedium text.primary, with a leading 16pt alert glyph in semantic.warning (on the glyph only).
  - The fixture threshold is 101, the server default. Also draw one specimen at 151, labelled "threshold 151 (not crossed)".
  - In the instrument row, the threshold number sits to the right of the rule's top end, and the track zone grows from 24pt to 40pt, in the alert cell only.
- 00a · SourceCaption: "● AirNow · nearest monitors · observed 7:00 AM". On alert, it reads "observed 4:00 PM". "●" stands for the drawn Official mark.

Component 00b-03: FourteenDayStrip. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PURPOSE (print it): The next two weeks at this address, drawn as a shape. The strip sits above list rows, and those rows are the real tap targets.
USED IN (print it): f5-today-calendar-strip, f7-today-widget, f7-widget-gallery, f7-widget-howto-sheet, f7-widget-tap-landing, f1-today-tab, x-place-file.
WEB-1440 CARD: 648px wide (616px of content), so each cell is 44px.
TYPE (two styles this component adds to the house scale; use them only as named):
- captionMedium 12/16/500. iOS AX5 → 43, Android 200% → 24.
- widgetCaption 11/16/400, widgets only. At AX sizes the widget drops to its text fallback (05), so widgetCaption has no AX5 or 200% size.

ANATOMY (on 01-anatomy, with a callout on every part)
- Header: the 00a · ScopeChip "Your household" (HOME A), then the summary label "Next 14 days: 6 items" in label 13/18 text.strong. The summary is the strip's one-sentence summary.
- Strip: 14 equal cells across the content width, today on the left. At 326pt the pitch is 23.3pt.
  - One track: radius sm 6, a 1px text.secondary keyline, and 1px text.secondary separators between cells.
  - Cell height 76pt, top to bottom: 6pt padding · up to 3 XS (12pt) ProvenanceMarks stacked with 4pt gaps (44pt) · a 4pt gap · a 16pt line reserved for "+N" · 6pt padding.
  - "+N" appears when a cell has 4 or more mark items (3 marks, then "+N"). It is in caption 12/16 text.strong (#F1F5F9 dark), because text.secondary on sunken is only 4.39:1. Otherwise the reserved line stays empty.
  - All marks use one ink, text.secondary at full opacity, centred in the cell. Marks never dim, in any state (C11).
- Cell fill: weekdays surface.sunken at 100%, weekends surface.sunken at 40%. Opacity marks the weekend, never hue, and the initials also name it (or "Sat–Sun" where there are no initials).
- Civic, state or county rule: a solid 4pt bar, full cell height, in text.strong. The bar is centred if the cell has no other marks. Otherwise it sits 2pt from the cell's left edge and the marks shift 3pt right. A bar never counts toward the 3-mark limit or "+N". A rule is never a dot. YearBand uses the same bar rule.
- Holiday move: the mark sits on the moved day. The usual day gets a struck ghost: the same shape at full text.secondary ink, crossed by a 1.5px diagonal strike in text.primary (#E5E7EB dark). The strike carries the meaning, and the DateRow names the move in words.
- Labels under the strip:
  - Row 1: weekday initials under every cell, in caption text.secondary: "M T W T F S S M T W T F S S". Draw them only where the pitch is 20pt or more. They are never spoken.
  - Row 2: anchors in captionMedium text.strong: "Today" left-aligned under cell 1 and "Mon 26 Oct" left-aligned under cell 8.

Component 00b-04: YearBand. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PURPOSE (print it): Twelve months of dated rules in four source lanes. It shows the same data as FourteenDayStrip at a longer zoom.
USED IN (print it): x-place-file, f7-today-widget, f7-widget-gallery.
WEB-1440 CARD: 880px wide (848px of content).
TYPE (two styles this component adds to the house scale; use them only as named):
- captionMedium 12/16/500. iOS AX5 → 43, Android 200% → 24.
- widgetCaption 11/16/400, widgets only. At AX sizes the widget drops to its text fallback (05), so widgetCaption has no AX5 or 200% size.

ANATOMY (on 01-anatomy-phone, with a callout on every part)
- Scope: the 00a · ScopeChip "Your household" (HOME A), above the summary header.
- Summary header, in label 13/18 text.strong: "Next 12 months: 10 dates. Next, in 4 days: Clark Public Utilities bill due Fri 23 Oct." The pickup rhythm is not counted as dates.
- Top line (16pt): "Today" in caption text.primary above the today rule, and "2027" above "Jan".
- Month columns: 12, current month first, in caption text.secondary: "Oct Nov Dec Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep". Phone: 326pt, so each column is 27.2pt.
- Lanes, in order: "You" · "Your city" · "Your county" · "Your state".
  - Phone stack per lane: a 16pt label line (captionMedium text.strong) · a 24pt lane · a 4pt gap. At 768px and wider, the labels sit in a 128px left column.
  - Lane track: surface.base fill, a 1px text.secondary keyline, radius xs 4, and 1px text.secondary month separators.
  - Paint order in each lane: lane fill · window wash · keyline and separators · rhythm ticks · today rule · marks, bars and numerals.
  - Marks, bars and numerals carry a 1pt halo that matches the fill beneath them, so the today rule stops short of them. On phones the rule (≈16.7pt) would otherwise cut across the Oct You tick (7.6–19.6pt). Callout this.
- Marks on phones: one group per month per lane.
  - Each group is an XS 12pt ProvenanceMark centred in the column. When the group has 2 or more items, add a count numeral in captionMedium text.primary, 1pt to the right of the mark.
  - A mixed-provenance group shows the hollow mark, and the rows list each item.
- Rules: county and state rules are solid 4pt bars, full lane height, in text.strong (the same rule as FourteenDayStrip). On phones a bar is centred in its month column, with a numeral when there are 2 or more.
- Collision rule (768px and wider only; exact-day placement happens only there):
  - Use drawn extents: a mark is 12px wide and a bar is 4px wide. Once a cluster holds 2 or more items, its numeral adds 1px plus the numeral's width (about 7px for one digit in captionMedium).
  - Work left to right within each lane. An item joins the current cluster if its left edge is less than 2px from the cluster's right edge (its mark or bar, plus the numeral once there is one). Otherwise the item starts a new cluster.
  - A cluster is drawn as one item at its earliest day, with its count numeral 1px to the right. Mixed provenance shows the hollow mark.
  - Rhythm ticks are not items and never merge.
  - Item centres: x = 128 + 60 × (month index + (day − 0.5) ÷ days in month), where Oct is month index 0.
- Today rule: 1.5px text.primary through all four lanes at 19 Oct (19/31 into Oct).
- Shaded 14-day window: 19 Oct–1 Nov across all lanes.
  - Wash: light surface.sunken; dark raised #1E293B (dark lanes are base #0F172A, so a sunken wash would vanish).
  - The wash carries the window, and the legend line under the band names it: "Shaded: next 14 days".
  - A 1px dashed text.secondary edge marks the end of 1 Nov. On phones that edge sits about 1.8pt past the Oct/Nov separator, so it also rises 4pt above the top lane as a tick, to tell it apart.
- Pickup rhythm, "Your city" lane:
  - Label line: "Your city", an XS hollow mark, and the caption "Pickup every Tuesday · city schedule" in caption text.secondary. At 768px and wider these sit in the label column under "Your city".
  - Ticks: 1.5 × 8pt in text.secondary, one per service week, centred vertically.
  - After the last published city calendar (Dec 2026), the Jan–Sep keyline turns dashed (3 on, 2 off). The caption "Projected after Dec 2026 (last published city calendar)" sits on its own 16pt caption line directly under the Your city lane.
  - Holiday moves on phones: that week's tick is 11pt tall with a 1.5px strike.
  - Holiday moves at 768px and wider: if the moved day is at least 14px from the usual day, the tick moves to the real day and a struck ghost (same shape, full ink) sits on the usual day. Otherwise use the phone form.
- The band reserves its full height while loading.
- Caption under the band, in text.secondary: "The same dates are listed below." Then come 00c · DateRow and 00c · FactRow rows, which are the table.
- Fixture data, HOME A:
  - You (all ticks): Oct "2" (Clark Public Utilities bill Fri 23 Oct; City of Vancouver water bill Wed 28 Oct) · Nov "2" (HOA dues Sun 1 Nov; Comcast bill Mon 2 Nov) · Dec (water-heater warranty ends Sat 12 Dec) · Mar "2" (lease notice deadline Mon 1 Mar; lease ends Wed 31 Mar).
  - Your city: the weekly Tuesday rhythm, on record, not confirmed. There is no holiday move in the published window.
  - Your county: a bar in Nov (property tax 2nd half due Mon 2 Nov; the row may add "moved from Sat 31 Oct").
  - Your state: bars in Oct (online or mail voter registration must arrive by Mon 26 Oct) and Nov (in person until 8:00 PM Tue 3 Nov).
  - Total: 10 dates (7 + 1 + 2).
