Component 00b-05: SlotMeter. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PURPOSE (print it): An honest, dated Founding Neighbor window. When anything is uncertain, it fails closed.
USED IN (print it): f9-founding-meter-preview, f9-block-founders-panel, f9-nearby-cells-map, f9-verification-promise-copy, f9-invite-rewards-card.
TYPE (one style this component adds to the house scale): bodyMedium 16/24/500. iOS AX5 → 53, Android 200% → 28.

ANATOMY (on 01-anatomy, with a callout on every part)
- Heading "Founding Neighbor" in bodyMedium text.primary.
- Segments: five bounded capsules, each 40 × 12pt, radius pill, with 4pt gaps (216pt in total). Taken segments come first, from the left.
  - Taken: solid primary.600 fill with a 1.5px primary.700 edge (#38BDF8 dark, per C6).
  - Open: surface.base fill with a 45° diagonal hatch (1.5px lines every 4pt) in text.secondary, and a 1.5px text.secondary edge.
  - Fixture: 2 taken, 3 open.
- Numeral label, 8pt right of the segments, in label 13/18 text.primary: "3 of 5 open". This count of open slots is the one sanctioned "N of M" here. It counts what is left and never measures progress.
- Elapsed bar, 8pt below the segments: 4 × 216pt, radius pill.
  - The elapsed part is solid text.secondary. The remaining part is an unfilled 1px text.secondary outline (never a border token).
  - The window opened Mon 5 Oct and closes Tue 27 Oct. TODAY is Mon 19 Oct, so the elapsed part is 138pt. Callout: "elapsed 138pt of 216pt; decorative".
  - The bar is decorative and hidden from assistive tech; the date pill carries the meaning.
- Date pill, 8pt below the bar: a neutral 24pt pill with a surface.sunken fill, holding a 12pt calendar glyph and "Closes Tue 27 Oct" in label 13/18, both in text.strong.
- RankBadge (part of this specimen, published only with SlotMeter). It appears only in V2 (HOME A), because a Block Founder rank cannot exist on an unclaimed place.
  - It always sits below the meter, at least 24pt away, never in the same row or sentence as the tier.
  - It is a separate squared shape: 128 × 64pt, radius md 8, surface.sunken fill, a 1px text.secondary edge, 12pt horizontal padding (104pt of text width) and 8pt vertical padding.
  - It holds the overline "BLOCK FOUNDER" in overline 11/16/600 caps +0.5 text.strong, then "#3" in h2 24/32/600 text.primary.
  - At default size the overline sits on one line (it measures about 91–100pt, inside 104pt). It breaks as "BLOCK / FOUNDER" only at AX sizes, where the badge grows vertically.
- R6 contrast table on 01: primary.600 fill on base, primary.700 on base, text.secondary on base, text.strong on sunken.

VARIANTS (row keys in brackets)
- V1 preview card [preview-card] (f9-founding-meter-preview, PLACE B): the heading, meter and date pill, plus the caption "A badge — no money or fee change. You can still claim this address." in bodySmall text.secondary. No RankBadge.
- V2 Block Founders panel [block-founders-panel] (f9-block-founders-panel, HOME A): the meter and date pill in the tier section, and the RankBadge "#3" in a separate rank section below.
- V3 wall line replacement [wall-line]: body text.primary only, with no meter: "3 Founding Neighbor slots are still open on this block."

STATES (column keys in brackets)
- open [open].
- closed [closed]: the meter is absent. Zero open slots counts as closed, so an empty meter is never drawn. In V2, only the tier section is removed. The rank section with "#3" stays, because the RankBadge is a separate earned shape that the founder already holds.
- lookup failed [lookup-failed]: the entire card is absent. In V2, both the tier and rank sections are removed, because the rank comes from the same failed lookup. In V3, the line is absent.
- Closed and lookup-failed cells are absence specimens per C5: draw the host context around the gap, plus the dashed gutter annotation box beside each removed section.

- Instead of a 2px elapsed bar, draw a 4pt bar, because a 1px outline cannot be drawn around a 2px shape.

PURPOSE (print it): Shows exactly where neighbours see a post, drawn at true scale from the server's stable public point.

ANATOMY (on 01-anatomy, with a callout on every part; the address is HOME A and the viewer is Maya Chen)
- V1 stack, top to bottom: map thumb · 8pt · caption · 8pt · controls. In context only, the hidden-from-neighbors row sits between the caption and the controls, with 8pt above and below it.
- Map thumb: 16:9, 326 × 183pt, radius md 8, 1px text.secondary edge. The frame is centred on the public pin.
  - Base map, neutral tokens only, no brand tint: land is surface.sunken; streets are 4pt surface.base lines with 1px text.secondary casing.
  - Street labels: caption 12/16 text.strong with a 2px surface.base halo: "NE 18th St", "NE 138th Ave", "NE 23rd St".
- Public pin: one 24pt teardrop in text.primary, 2px surface.base halo, 6pt surface.base centre.
- Pin label chip, above the pin: a pill in surface.base, 1px text.secondary edge, shadow md, reading exactly "What neighbors see" in label 13/18 text.primary.
- Scale bar, bottom left, on an 80% surface.base plate: a 1.5px text.primary line with end ticks; labels "0", "0.1", "0.2 mi" in caption 12/16 text.primary on the plate. The thumb spans about 0.8 mi, so 0.2 mi = 81pt.
- Caption, bodySmall text.primary, the map's one-sentence summary, used exactly: "Neighbors see your posts at this spot, the same spot every time, about 0.3 mi from your address."

  - Each button is 44 × 44pt on iOS and web and 48 × 48dp on Android: radius md 8, surface.base fill, 1px text.secondary edge, 20pt text.primary glyph. The accessible names are the words below.
  - One two-row cluster at every size. Left edge of the content width: a zoom column, "Zoom in" (+) above "Zoom out" (−), 8pt apart. Right edge: a 3 × 2 arrow pad with 8pt gaps. Top row: "Move map up" (↑) in the middle slot. Bottom row: "Move map left" (←), "Move map down" (↓), "Move map right" (→).
  - Size: the pad is 148pt wide on iOS and web (3 × 44 + 2 × 8) and 160dp on Android. The cluster needs at least 208pt (224dp) with a 16pt minimum gap between column and pad, so it fits 326pt. It is 96pt tall on iOS and web and 104dp on Android.
  - Disabled buttons: fill unchanged, still focusable, with a reason. Light: glyph and edge in text.muted. Dark: glyph and edge in #475569 (an added dark value, listed on Notes D), so disabled stays distinct from the enabled #94A3B8 edge. Disabled controls are exempt from the contrast minimums; the reason text carries the meaning.
  - Focus order: Zoom in, Zoom out, Move map up, Move map left, Move map down, Move map right, then List cells when present.
- Cells-map parts (V3):
  - V3 stack, top to bottom: map 326 × 326 (the same base map at the same zoom, with streets and street labels, no pin, no chip, scale bar bottom left) · 8pt · summary line · 4pt · FreshnessLine · 8pt · controls · 8pt · List cells.

  - The user's cell gets a 2px primary.600 inner outline inside its rectangle (the contract calls it a ring; #38BDF8 in dark mode), and "Your cell" in caption text.primary, centred 4pt below its bucket label.
  - "List cells": a text button (primary.700; #38BDF8 in dark mode), left-aligned, 44pt tall (48dp on Android). The V3 controls block is therefore 148pt tall on iOS and web (96 + 8 + 44) and 160dp on Android (104 + 8 + 48).

  - text.secondary on base · text ("Simplified map") and edges · 4.5:1
  - text.secondary on sunken · outline (map edge, street casing) · 3:1
  - text.strong on sunken · text (street labels) · 4.5:1
  - text.primary on sunken · text and pin · 4.5:1
  - primary.700 on base · text ("See the spot", "List cells") · 4.5:1
  - primary.600 on the 70% base cell fill (light) · outline · 3:1
  - #38BDF8 on the dark cell fill · outline · 3:1

Component 00b-07: FactCount. Follow the board rules from the setup message. This is the last component on the board.

PURPOSE (print it): States how much is on file for the address, without implying that anything is missing.
USED IN (print it): x-place-file, f11-keeper-strip, f1-claim-receipt.

FRAMES: 02 cells are drawn on a 358pt iOS card. Draw the target outline around the whole block (at least 44 × 44pt; the block height when taller).

ANATOMY (on 01-anatomy, with a callout on every part)
- A vertical block, at most 160pt wide. The place file header and the keeper strip use the same geometry.
- Line 1: the integer in h3 20/28/600 text.primary (the contract gives only its weight, "label weight" = 600; the h3 size is a design choice, see Notes B), a 4pt gap, then "on file" in caption 12/16 text.secondary, sharing one baseline.
- Line 2, 6pt below line 1: category pips, one labelled pip for each category that has anything known, in this fixed order: Place · Dates · Money · People · Proof.
  - Pip: height = its text line height + 4pt (20pt at default), radius pill, surface.sunken fill, captionMedium 12/16/500 text.strong (9.37:1), 8pt horizontal padding, 4pt gaps. captionMedium is the board's weight-500 caption and scales as caption (AX5 43, 200% 24).
  - Pips wrap to a further line when needed, 4pt below the previous pip line. For the fixture, Place · Dates · Money fills the first pip line and People wraps, so V1 and V2 are 78pt tall (28 + 6 + 20 + 4 + 20).
  - A pip is always a word, never a bare dot, so categories are carried by words, not colour.
- Unknown categories draw nothing (see INSTEAD OF).
- Target: the whole block is one target of at least 44pt (48dp on Android, 44px on web), extended beyond the visible block if needed. Tapping it opens the place file; inside x-place-file, it scrolls to the list.
- Fixture: HOME A shows "14 on file" with Place · Dates · Money · People.
- Contrast table on 01, R6 rows: text.primary on base · text · 4.5:1; text.secondary on base · text · 4.5:1; text.strong on sunken · text · 4.5:1. In dark mode, pips on a dark raised card use dark sunken #0F172A; pips on dark base use dark raised #1E293B (R5).

SetupWebiOSAndroid0 artboards2,431 words

Board rules for every component on this board. Send first; draws nothing.

Setup 00c-00: Foundations board 00c, Rows and lists.

Use the Pantopus house style pasted above. This project is Foundations board 00c, "Rows and lists". Read this message, then reply. Draw nothing yet.

WHAT THIS BOARD IS FOR
This is a component specimen board with no screens. I will send one component per message, in this order: DateRow, FactRow, FirstWeekRow, BillRow, MemberRow, InviteRow, NotificationRow, TextActionRow, LockedActionRow, GrantLimitList, InlineErrorRow, ThumbnailRail. Each component message is that component's complete specification. This message holds only the rules for all twelve, R1 to R14 ("the board rules").
Later screen projects will use these components by exact name and key, with no other reference, so every specimen must be complete, exact and labelled. ATTACH: none.

PUBLISH
When I accept a component, I add it to the published Pantopus design system under its exact name above. Its variants and states are published under the printed keys from its grid (R7), e.g. DateRow variant "deadline-voter", state "highlighted-arrival". Never publish a drawing labelled "stand-in" (R11); those components come from their own Foundations boards.

HOW EACH COMPONENT TURN WORKS
- Each component message ends with ARTBOARDS, a BATCH PLAN and DONE WHEN. Draw only what the BATCH PLAN lists for the current turn, then stop and wait for "continue". Never start a component before its message arrives.
- Before stopping, check the batch against DONE WHEN and name anything missing.
- If a component message and these rules disagree, the component message wins; note it on Notes.
- Ask a question only if two readings would produce materially different components.

R1. ARTBOARDS
- Name each artboard "00c · <ComponentName> · <NN-what> · <light|dark>", exactly as the component's ARTBOARDS list gives it (this replaces the house style's surface naming). Show the name as a visible label above the frame in caption 12/16 text.secondary.
- Each component gets exactly five artboards, in this order:
  01-anatomy · light: one specimen at 2x with numbered callouts (R3), then five labelled text panels: ACCESSIBILITY, COPY RULES, PLATFORMS, INSTEAD OF, USED IN.
  02-grid · light: the variant × state grid at 1x (R7).
  03-ax5-200-greyscale · light: at the top, two large-text columns labelled "iOS · AX5 (body 53pt)" and "Android · 200%" (Android 14 nonlinear scaling), per R9. Below, full width at 1x, a greyscale (0% saturation) copy of the whole 02 grid, per R10.
  04-in-context · light: the crops the component names (R13).
  05-grid · dark: the 02 grid in the same layout in dark tokens (R5), plus the 1x anatomy specimen in dark at top left.
- The last artboard in the project is "00c · Notes" (R14).

R2. CANVAS AND UNITS
- Artboards are at least 1440 wide, on surface.app (dark: dark app). Grow them to fit cells at 1x; never scale a cell down.
- 1pt = 1dp = 1px. Callouts give iOS pt, or all three where they differ ("44pt / 48dp / 44px").
- Row frames unless a cell says otherwise: iOS 393pt with 16pt side margins (361pt content); Android 412dp (380dp content); web-390 390px (358px content); web-1440 a 720px list column.
- Spacing and radii by name (spacing.2 = 8, spacing.3 = 12, spacing.4 = 16; md 8, lg 12).

R3. CALLOUTS
- Outside the component: a numbered circle (1px text.secondary outline), a 1px text.secondary leader, and a caption with size and token, e.g. "② title · body 16/24/400 · text.primary". Numbers match the component's ANATOMY list.
- Callouts never overlap the component. Spacing uses 1px dimension lines ("16pt · spacing.4").
- Draw every target as a dashed 1px text.secondary rectangle labelled "target 44pt / 48dp / 44px".
- Every 01-anatomy has a "web menu" callout (R12), worded as the component message says.

R4. TYPE AND LIGHT TOKENS
- Type scale only: body 16/24/400 · bodyMedium 16/24/500 · bodySmall 14/20/400 · bodySmallMedium 14/20/500 · label 13/18/600 · caption 12/16/400 · captionMedium 12/16/500 · overline 11/16/600 caps +0.5. SF Pro on iOS, Roboto on Android, system-ui on web. Amounts use tabular figures.
- Token names only, never hex on a component. Light values are in the house style; this board also uses primary.50, primary.700, errorBg, infoBg and identity.home.
- text.muted appears nowhere on this board.
- Secondary-role text (captions, "Not set", disabled labels, reason captions) is text.secondary on base, raised and app, and text.strong on surface.sunken and errorBg, where text.secondary fails (R6).
- Text buttons and links are bodySmallMedium primary.700 unless a component says otherwise.
- Semantic hues and identity.home go on glyphs and rules only, never on text.
- Border tokens are decoration. Row separators are 1px border.default hairlines inset 16pt from the leading edge, and no row relies on a hairline as its only edge. Any edge that carries meaning uses text.secondary ink.

R5. DARK MODE (every 05)
Dark tokens: surface.base #0F172A, raised #1E293B, sunken #0F172A (same as base), app #020617; text.primary #E5E7EB, text.strong #F1F5F9, text.secondary #94A3B8; border.default #1F2937, strong #374151, subtle #1E293B, focus #38BDF8. Links and text buttons use dark border.focus.
Dark has no infoBg, errorBg, primary.50, primary.700 or semantic tokens, and dark sunken equals base. Use exactly these substitutes, and record each use on Notes:
- D1 Highlight: dark raised wash plus the 4pt leading bar in dark border.focus. On a row already on raised (D3), the bar alone.
- D2 Write-failure fill: dark raised plus a 1.5px error border.
- D3 A row on sunken in light sits on dark raised, with dark text.strong.
- D4 Any sunken fill (skeleton bars, avatars, chip fills, thumbnail slots, a disabled filled button) becomes dark raised on a base row and dark border.strong on a raised row; text inside is dark text.strong.
- D5 Selection: dark raised plus a 1.5px dark border.focus edge plus a leading check in dark border.focus. Never primary.50.
- D6 Non-link primary.700 graphics (progress rings, spinners, unread dot) use dark border.focus; ring tracks use dark border.strong.
- D7 Semantic glyph hues and the identity.home rule keep their light values, on glyphs and rules only. Caption the R6 ratio beside the first occurrence on each 05.
- D8 Any card gets a 1px dark text.secondary keyline, because dark border.default on raised is 1.00:1. Caption its ratio beside the first occurrence.
Increase Contrast: no separate artboard. Every R6 check must also hold under Increase Contrast; the only change is that light cards get the same text.secondary keyline as D8. Write this once as a caption on each 05.

R7. GRID LABELS AND KEYS
- Variants are rows, labelled at the left in label 13/18 text.strong. States are columns, labelled at the top in overline 11/16/600.
- Each label reads exactly "<code> · <key>" with the codes and keys from the component message (e.g. "V3a · deadline-voter", "S2a · highlighted-arrival"). Under it, print "key: <key>" in caption 12/16 text.secondary.
- Keys are lowercase and hyphenated, with no spaces, no "/", no fixture string and no date. Publish names use keys only.
- Under every cell, in caption 12/16 text.secondary, print exactly "<ComponentName> · <variant key> · <state key>" (e.g. "DateRow · deadline-voter · done").
- Draw only the cells in GRID CELLS. Every other position stays empty canvas: no frame, no label, no "n/a".
- An n/a cell appears only where a component writes "n/a": a plain cell reading "n/a — <reason>" in caption text.secondary, with the normal cell caption. Never draw a ghost component there.

R8. TARGETS, FOCUS, HIGHLIGHT, SELECTION, DISABLED
- Targets: 44pt iOS, 48dp Android with 8dp gaps, 44px web. A ProvenanceMark, glyph or dot is never a target by itself.
- Focus: a 2px border.focus ring 2px outside the whole row. When a row holds a separate target (link, overflow, Retry, Resend, Add, dismiss), focus on it rings that target only.
- Highlight (arrival from a notification): an infoBg wash across the row plus a 4pt border.focus bar on the leading edge, full height. No outline, never a check. If the row has a 2px identity.home rule, the bar sits directly inside it. In an "on arrival" frame the focus ring is also drawn 2px outside the row, so bar and ring never touch. Dark: D1.
- Selection: primary.50 fill plus a leading check glyph. Dark: D5.
- Focus, highlight and selection must look different. Wherever a grid has a highlighted or selected cell, a focused cell sits directly beside it.
- Disabled text actions look the same everywhere: label in text.secondary (text.strong on sunken, per R4), never primary.700 or text.muted, still focusable, with a reason caption directly under it in caption 12/16 (same colour rule). Disabled filled buttons: surface.sunken fill, text.strong label (dark: D4).
- Disabled controls stay in the accessibility tree with their reason as a hint.

R9. AX5 / 200% (every 03)
- Text wraps and never truncates, except a field the component names as truncating at default sizes only.
- Side-by-side pairs stack. Trailing elements (amount, mark, chevron, text action) move below the text block, aligned to its leading edge, and keep their targets.
- Leading glyphs and marks scale with the text; ProvenanceMark keeps its shape. Row heights grow; stated heights are minimums.

R10. GREYSCALE (every 03)
Draw the whole 02 grid desaturated, same labels and captions. Beside it, caption each variant or state with its non-colour cue, e.g. "done = tick glyph + 'You marked this done'". A cell that reads only through colour is a defect: fix the component.

R11. SHARED STAND-INS
If the published design system has one of these, use it; otherwise draw this stand-in, labelled "stand-in". Components may add their own.
- ProvenanceMark: OFFICIAL = solid disc; ON RECORD, NOT CONFIRMED = ring, stroke at least 1.5px; YOU ADDED = solid disc with a knocked-out tick (a cut-out, never a second colour). Ink text.secondary (dark: dark text.secondary). S = 16pt in rows; XS = 12pt minimum. Spoken "official", "on record, not confirmed", "you added this". Filled vs hollow means provenance only. Every other check on this board is a bare stroke, never a disc.
- Legend line: "● Official · ○ On record, not confirmed · ✓ You added this" in caption text.secondary, or the word beside the first mark.
- ScopeChip: pill, 24pt, surface.sunken fill (dark: D4), 12pt glyph plus label 13/18 text.strong. Exactly "Saved place · Only you" (person glyph) or "Your household" (house glyph), spoken "Visible to only you" / "Visible to your household". Sentences exactly "Only you will see this." / "Everyone in this household will see this."; where finance access differs, name the people ("You and Sam can see these"), never "Everyone". When the chip opens the scope control, draw its 44pt / 48dp target.
- StatusChip: pill, 24pt, captionMedium, surface.sunken fill (dark: D4), text.strong; any semantic hue on a leading glyph only; one per row.
- InlineUndo: the row collapses in place to "<what happened> · Undo", announced with role=status. Undo is focusable, 44pt, and stays until the user leaves the screen. No countdown.
- WarmingSkeleton: surface.sunken bars (dark: D4) in the final geometry and height, no text, announced once as "Loading" (aria-busy on web); static under Reduce Motion.
- FreshnessLine / OfflineNotice: caption text.secondary, e.g. "You're offline · as of 5:52 PM" (invented). No banner colour.

R12. PLATFORMS AND THE WEB MENU
- Unless a component's PLATFORMS says otherwise, write "No platform differences" in its panel.
- Custom actions are VoiceOver custom actions on iOS and TalkBack custom actions on Android.
- On web, custom actions that are not already visible buttons get a row menu button: a 20px ellipsis in a 44px target at the row's trailing edge. An existing overflow button or visible buttons already are the web menu; never add a second. Draw it in every web crop where it applies.

R13. IN-CONTEXT CROPS (every 04)
- Label each crop "<surface id> · <ios|android|web-390|web-1440>". Show only enough host to place the component: outlines, section titles, neighbouring rows.
- Every crop that shows a ProvenanceMark also shows the legend line and the place's ScopeChip: "Your household" for Home A, "Saved place · Only you" for Place B.

R14. FIXTURES, MOTION, NOTES
- Use the house-style FIXTURES. TODAY is Mon 19 Oct 2026, 6:10 PM Pacific; relative counts come from it. Dates always show the weekday ("Fri 23 Oct"), never numeric formats, never "midnight". Emails use @example.com. No percentage or completion fraction is drawn on any specimen, callout or crop; an INSTEAD OF panel may name one only as the pattern to avoid.
- Motion: highlights fade within 300ms. Under Reduce Motion they cross-fade, spinners are removed and in-progress labels stay as static text. Idle loops stop within 5s.
- "00c · Notes" is the last artboard. Create it when a BATCH PLAN first says so; update it whenever a BATCH PLAN says so. One line per item.
  Board section first: each D1–D8 with the components that used it and the D7/D8 ratios; the Increase Contrast note; the R11 stand-ins you drew; any string you added that no message lists; any state you could not draw, and why.
  Then one section per component, in delivery order, under its exact name, with the lists its message gives: Invented strings · Fixture deltas · Contract conflicts (each "drawn as X instead of contract Y") · Assumptions.

Reply 'ready' and wait for the first component.

Component 00c-01: DateRow. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PUBLISH NAME: DateRow. This message is the complete DateRow specification.

PURPOSE (print at the top of 01). One dated fact in a list. Its row grammar is shared by the 14-day strip list, the calendar agenda, the place file Dates section and reminder rows.

USED IN (panel): f5-today-calendar-strip · f3-household-calendar · x-place-file · x-date-sheet · f3-household-notifications · f7-today-widget.

EXTRA STAND-INS FOR THIS COMPONENT (label each "stand-in", per R11)
- KindGlyph: a 24pt line icon with a 2pt stroke in text.strong, with one distinct drawing per kind: garbage, recycling, garbage+recycling, notice deadline, warranty ends, HOA dues, property-tax due, property-tax appeal, voter registration. Never one generic calendar icon.
- SourceCaption: caption 12/16 text.secondary, "authority · scope · as-of". It wraps and never ellipsises the authority.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw V3a at 2x for callouts ①–⑦ and ⑩. Beside it, draw V3c in S3 (done) at 2x for callouts ⑧ and ⑨.
① Row: minimum height 56pt, padding 16pt horizontal and 12pt vertical, on surface.base. The whole row is the target: draw the dashed target rectangle around it.
② Leading KindGlyph, 24pt, text.strong, top-aligned with the title, with a 12pt (spacing.3) gap after it.
③ Title: body 16/24/400, text.primary. It wraps and is never truncated.
④ Line 2: caption 12/16 text.secondary, the relative date then the absolute date, e.g. "in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct". "Tonight", "Today" and "Tomorrow" stand alone, with no absolute date after them. An approximate date reads "about Dec 2026".
⑤ SourceCaption short form (authority · scope). It continues line 2 after a middot, or wraps to line 3.
⑥ Trailing ProvenanceMark S (16pt), vertically centred, with 8pt (spacing.2) between it and the text. It is not a target.
⑦ Optional chip after the title reading "Statewide — WA", in ScopeChip geometry (24pt pill, surface.sunken fill, label 13/18 text.strong) with a 12pt state-outline glyph. It states coverage, not visibility.
⑧ Annual rows and self-entered rows: a 2px identity.home rule on the leading edge, full row height, plus a recurrence caption on the last line in caption text.secondary ("Every year", "Every month" or "Does not repeat").
⑨ Done tick: a 16pt stroke check before the title. It is a bare stroke, not a disc, so it cannot be mistaken for the YOU ADDED mark.
⑩ Web menu callout: "web menu: a row menu button (20px ellipsis, 44px target) after the mark, holding Edit · Remind me · Where this comes from · Mark done".

VARIANTS (rows; label each "<code> · <key>")
V1 pickup. Home A as of TODAY, before Maya confirmed her pickup day. The title names the bins.
- V1a · pickup-both: garbage+recycling glyph · title "Recycling and garbage" · line 2 "Tomorrow · Waste Connections · city schedule" · hollow mark.
- V1b · pickup-garbage: garbage glyph · "Garbage only" · "in 8 days · Tue 27 Oct · Waste Connections · city schedule" · hollow mark.

V3 deadline. The weekday is always shown, and received-by deadlines say "must arrive by".

- V3b · deadline-notice: notice deadline glyph · "Tell your landlord in writing by Mon 1 Mar 2027" · "in 133 days · Mon 1 Mar 2027 · Lease ends Wed 31 Mar 2027" · last line "Does not repeat · Reminder Sat 30 Jan 2027" · YOU ADDED mark · identity.home rule.

- V4 · conditional-rule: property-tax appeal glyph · "Property-tax appeal window" · "Closes Thu 1 Jul 2027, or 60 days after your value notice was mailed" · "Clark County Board of Equalization · county-wide" · last line "Every year" · filled mark · identity.home rule.

STATES (columns, in this order: S1, S2a, S2b, SF, S3, S4)
- S1 · default.
- S2 · highlighted: arrival from a notification, per R8 (dark: D1), with accessibility focus moved onto the row. Drawn as two columns:

GRID CELLS (02 and 05; 26 cells)
- S1 and S3: V1a, V1b, V2, V3a, V3b, V3c, V4, V5, V5x and V6 (20 cells).

- S4: one cell, in the V6 row: a three-row list of V1a, [absent V6], V3a. The rows above and below close the gap, with no placeholder and no ghost row. An annotation arrow outside the list reads "row absent: viewer lacks permission" (1 cell).
- Outside the V3a S3 cell, annotate: "done stays Only you".

DARK (05)
- Rows stay on dark surface.base. Highlight uses D1. The "Statewide — WA" chip fill uses D4. Marks and the done tick use dark text.secondary; each KindGlyph uses dark text.strong.
- The identity.home rule keeps its hue (D7). Beside the first one, caption "identity.home on dark base 5.42:1".

AX5 / 200% (03): draw V3a and V6 in both columns.
- The title wraps to as many lines as it needs.

- The amount and the mark move below the text block: the amount first, then the mark, scaled to about 28pt.

- The identity.home rule stays full height.

GREYSCALE (03 captions)
- provenance = disc vs ring vs disc with knocked-out tick.
- done = stroke tick + "You marked this done".
- highlighted = 4pt leading bar.
- annual = 2px rule + "Every year".
- kind = KindGlyph shape.

ACCESSIBILITY (panel)
- The whole row is one element and one target (minimum 56pt), read in visual order. The mark and the glyph are not targets.
- Spoken pattern: "<title>, <line 2 as shown>, <authority, scope>, <mark name>". The label speaks only the dates the row shows, so "Tomorrow" is spoken as "tomorrow" with no absolute date. Example: "Recycling and garbage, tomorrow, Waste Connections city schedule, on record, not confirmed."
- Done rows start with "You marked this done". Done stays Only you.
- Custom actions: Edit · Remind me · Where this comes from · Mark done. On web they sit in the ⑩ row menu button.
- Non-colour encoding: the glyph shape carries the kind, the mark shape carries provenance, the leading bar carries highlight, and the words carry done.
- Contrast: text at least 4.5:1; mark at least 3:1 (text.secondary on base, 4.83:1).

COPY RULES (panel)
- For deadlines, the title names the action: "Tell your landlord in writing by Mon 1 Mar 2027".
- Received-by deadlines say "must arrive by".
- Dates are spelled out with the weekday ("Mon 26 Oct"), never 10/26/2026.
- Beyond tomorrow, the relative count comes first: "in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct". Conditional rules (V4) are exempt from the relative count.
- Source captions carry a scope word: "Clark County Treasurer · county-wide".
- Pickup titles use exactly "Recycling and garbage" or "Garbage only".
- Holiday moves read "moved to Fri 27 Nov", never "delayed" or "cancelled".
- "I did this" reads "You marked this done" and stays Only you.

PLATFORMS (panel): No platform differences, except that web adds the ⑩ row menu button (R12).

INSTEAD OF (panel)
- Instead of red text or an overdue chip on an annual date that has passed, draw the next occurrence with its "Every year" caption. Annual dates never inherit overdue red.
- Instead of one generic calendar icon for every row, draw the specific KindGlyph. The glyph is what tells kinds apart without colour.
- Instead of a greyed placeholder row for a date the viewer may not see, draw nothing. A ghost row leaks that something exists.
- Instead of a numeric date like 10/26/2026, draw "Mon 26 Oct". The weekday is what people plan by.

IN CONTEXT (04): three crops, each with the legend line and the ScopeChip (R13).
1. f5-today-calendar-strip · ios, Home A: ScopeChip "Your household"; a card (radius lg) holding a 14-cell strip drawn only as a plain outline (the strip is specified on another board), above rows V1a, V3a and V6; a foot row "+ Add a date"; the legend line. Annotate the strip: "strip cells are not targets; the rows below are".

3. f3-household-calendar · android, Home A: ScopeChip "Your household"; an agenda with the day header "Tue 20 Oct" and row V1a in S2a; the legend line.

PUBLISH NAME: FactRow. This message is the complete FactRow specification.

PURPOSE (print at the top of 01). One row per fact in the place file and in settings. The fact is known, missing, or not available at this tier.

USED IN (panel): x-place-file · f6-home-basics-rows · f1-today-tab · f3-household-block · f9-verification-promise-copy · f4-notification-settings.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw three specimens at 2x, stacked: V1a (known, chevron), V2a (missing, "Add") and the ⑦ disclosure row.
① Row: minimum height 56pt, padding 16pt horizontal, on surface.base, content vertically centred.
② Label: bodySmall 14/20, text.secondary, above the value.
③ Value: body 16/24, text.primary.
④ ProvenanceMark S (16pt) after the value, with an 8pt (spacing.2) gap. It is not a target.
⑤ Trailing element: either a chevron (16pt, text.secondary) or a text action in bodySmallMedium primary.700 (dark: dark border.focus), e.g. "Add".
⑥ Missing form: the label, then an ask sentence in body text.primary, then the text action "Add".
⑦ Disclosure row "More you can add (5)" with a chevron, 44pt minimum. At most 3 promoted asks show per screen; the rest sit under this row.
⑧ Target rule callout. On rows with a chevron, the whole row is the target. On rows with a text action (missing, declined, permission-disabled), the text action is a separate 44pt / 48dp / 44px button and the row itself is not a target. Rows with neither (V3 and V8) are not targets. Draw the dashed target on each specimen accordingly: around the V1a row, and around "Add" only on V2a.
⑨ Web menu callout: "no custom actions; no row menu button".

VARIANTS (rows; label each "<code> · <key>"). Each cell belongs to the place named.
V1 known:
- V1a · known-flood (any address): label "Flood zone" · value "Zone X — minimal flood hazard" · filled mark · chevron.
- V1b · known-pickup-unconfirmed (Home A as of TODAY): label "Pickup day" · value "Tuesday · Waste Connections" · hollow mark · chevron.
- V1d · known-pickup-confirmed (Home A, fixture delta: after Maya confirmed Tuesday): label "Pickup day" · value "Tuesday · Waste Connections" · filled mark · chevron.

- V3 · not-at-tier (Place B): label "People who live here" · value "Claim this address first" in text.secondary · no action, no chevron and no mark.
- V4 · done-ask (Home A, same fixture delta as V1d), drawn quiet: a 16pt bare stroke check (not a disc, so it cannot be mistaken for the YOU ADDED mark) · "Pickup day set · Tuesday", all in text.secondary · chevron.
V5 declined (Home A before Sam joined; fixture delta):

PLATFORMS (panel): No platform differences.

INSTEAD OF (panel)
- Instead of a red X or red text for a missing fact, draw the ask sentence with "Add". Missing is an invitation, not an error.
- Instead of a score, percentage or "3 of 6" on the place file, draw plain rows and the "More you can add (5)" disclosure. Counts of completion create pressure.

PUBLISH NAME: FirstWeekRow. This message is the complete FirstWeekRow specification.

PURPOSE (print at the top of 01). The single pointer on Today to the next first-week ask. It comes from a bounded set of steps that the person has already started.

USED IN (panel): f1-today-tab · x-place-file · f4-briefing-optin-card. (f4-briefing-optin-card is not cropped on 04: it only hosts the row, so it adds nothing beyond the f1-today-tab crop.)

FIXTURE DELTA (applies to every FirstWeekRow specimen). The specimens show Place B (Jordan Lee) on Tue 13 Oct 2026, 3 days after the Sat 10 Oct save. The 7-day activation window runs Sun 11 Oct through Sat 17 Oct and closes after Sat 17 Oct. The hidden variant (V2) shows Mon 19 Oct, when the window has closed. Place B's pickup day is known (Thursday, City of Camas); its pickup frequency is Not set.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw V1a at 2x.
① One row, 48pt high at default sizes: padding 16pt horizontal and 12pt vertical (12 + 24 + 12 = 48), on surface.base. At default sizes the step text is one line; if it wraps, the row grows and the dismiss button stays top-aligned.
② Text in bodyMedium 16/24, text.primary: "Next: set your pickup day →". The arrow is part of the link. The whole row except the dismiss button is the link target: draw its dashed target.
③ Trailing dismiss button: a 16pt close glyph in text.secondary inside a 44pt / 48dp target, with 8dp between it and the link target. Draw its dashed target too.
④ Callout listing the bounded set: "Save (already done) · Pickup day · Reminder or widget · One date or person".
⑤ Callout: "Only steps reachable at the current tier are counted. Verify, profile and photo are never steps."
⑥ Callout: "Shown for 7 days (the activation window)."
⑦ Web menu callout: "the visible dismiss button is the only extra action; no row menu button".

VARIANTS (rows; label each "<code> · <key>")
- V1a · next-pickup: "Next: set your pickup day →". For Place B this step means confirming the known day and setting the frequency.
- V1b · next-widget: "Next: put today on your home screen →" (invented). It may wrap at 361pt; if it does, apply the ① rule.
- V2 · hidden (set complete, dismissed, or window closed): draw an outline of the Place B Today section stack (ScopeChip, pickup section, air section) with no FirstWeekRow and no gap where it would be, plus the annotation "hidden: set complete, dismissed, or 7 days passed".

STATES (columns, in this order: S1, SFl, SFd, S2)
- S1 · default.
- SFl · focused-link: the focus ring around the link target only.
- SFd · focused-dismiss: the focus ring around the dismiss button only.
- S2 · dismissed (stored on the server): the row collapses in place to the InlineUndo "Hidden from Today · Undo" (invented). Undo has a 44pt target and stays until the user leaves Today. There is no countdown.

GRID CELLS (02 and 05; 7 cells)
- S1: V1a, V1b and V2 (V2 is one cell, in the S1 column).
- SFl and SFd: V1a, side by side, each ringing only its own target (2 cells).
- S2: V1a and V1b (2 cells).

DARK (05)
- The row sits on dark surface.base. Text is dark text.primary, the close glyph dark text.secondary, and "Undo" dark border.focus.
- No substitutes beyond the token swap are needed. Add the Increase Contrast caption (R5).

AX5 / 200% (03): draw V1a in S1 and V1a in S2, in both columns.
- The text wraps to two or more lines, and the arrow stays at the end of the text.
- The dismiss button stays top-aligned at the trailing edge and keeps its target (overrides R9: a dismiss control stays top-trailing).
- The row grows beyond 48pt.
- In S2, "Undo" wraps below "Hidden from Today" and keeps its 44pt / 48dp target.

GREYSCALE (03 captions)
- next step = the words; no colour is used.
- dismissed = "Hidden from Today · Undo".
- hidden = absence, carried by the annotation.

ACCESSIBILITY (panel)
- The row is one link: "Next: set your pickup day. Link."
- Dismiss is a separate button, "Dismiss next step" (invented), and is also offered as a custom action on the link.
- Undo is announced with role=status and is focusable.
- Targets: the link row is 48pt; the dismiss button is 44pt / 48dp / 44px, 8dp from the link.

COPY RULES (panel)
- Name only the next step, in sentence case, verb first. Never show a count or fraction of steps.
- The row shows for 7 days, matching the activation window.
- Step strings come from the set: "set your pickup day", "put today on your home screen" (invented), "add one date that matters" (invented).

PLATFORMS (panel): No platform differences.

INSTEAD OF (panel)
- Instead of "3 of 6" or any denominator, draw "Next: <step> →". Naming the next step moves people without pressure.
- Instead of counting verify, profile or photo, draw only the four set steps reachable at the viewer's tier. A step you cannot do is not a step.
- Instead of a checklist card, draw this single 48pt row. The full list lives in the place file.

IN CONTEXT (04): two crops (R13).
1. f1-today-tab · ios, Place B: ScopeChip "Saved place · Only you"; then V1a; then the pickup section outline, showing "Pickup day" with a hollow mark, and the legend line.
2. x-place-file · web-390, Place B: ScopeChip "Saved place · Only you"; the same step drawn as two published FactRow variants: V1c (label "Pickup day" · value "Thursday · City of Camas" · hollow mark · chevron), then V2b (label "Pickup frequency" · value "Not set" in text.secondary · action "Add"). Annotation: "same set, same storage". Add the legend line (R13). No row menu button.

NOTES (add a "FirstWeekRow" section to 00c · Notes)
- Invented strings: every string marked (invented) above.
- Fixture deltas: specimens on Tue 13 Oct 2026, 3 days after the Sat 10 Oct save; the 7-day window runs Sun 11 Oct through Sat 17 Oct · V2 on Mon 19 Oct, after the window closed · the pickup step for Place B covers both confirming the known day (FactRow V1c) and setting the frequency (FactRow V2b) · the set step "One date or person" is drawn as "add one date that matters" because the person half is locked for Place B at T1 ("Claim this address first") and is not counted.

The contract's "no-fraction" variant is drawn as V1a and V1b · link target drawn as the whole row minus the dismiss button (contract: whole-row link), so dismiss can have its own target.

PUBLISH NAME: InviteRow. This message is the complete InviteRow specification.

PURPOSE (print at the top of 01). A pending invitation or invite link, with its expiry and a one-tap fix.

USED IN (panel): f3-members-roster · x-place-file · f3-invite-composer · f3-invite-banner.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw V1 at 2x under its "PENDING" overline.
① Row: minimum 56pt, in a "PENDING" group (overline 11/16 text.secondary) that only managers see. Quieter than people rows: no avatar on any variant.
② Leading mail glyph, 16pt, text.secondary.
③ Line 1, the recipient: bodySmall 14/20 text.primary, "priya@example.com" or a username such as "@priya".
④ Line 2, the caption: caption 12/16 text.secondary, "Member · sent Mon 12 Oct · Expires in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct". It runs the full text width under ⑤ and ⑥ and wraps at a middot when it has to.
⑤ "Resend" text button, bodySmallMedium primary.700 (dark: dark border.focus), trailing and aligned to line 1, with a 44pt target. Draw its dashed target.
⑥ Overflow button (44pt / 48dp) holding Cancel · Extend, trailing, 8dp after Resend. Draw its dashed target.
⑦ Web menu callout: "the ⑥ overflow is the web row menu button; rows without an overflow use their visible buttons; no second menu".

VARIANTS (rows; label each "<code> · <key>")
- V1 · pending-email: as in the anatomy.
- V1u · pending-username: V1 with the recipient "@priya".
- V2 · expiring (fixture delta: shown on Sun 25 Oct): V1 with the caption "Member · sent Mon 12 Oct · Expires tomorrow · Mon 26 Oct". The expiry is words in text.secondary, not tinted.
- V3 · needs-reissue: a 16pt warning glyph replaces the mail glyph (hue on the glyph only; dark: D7). Line 1: the recipient, with ⑥ trailing. Line 2: "Needs reissue — your household's invite rules changed" in bodySmall text.primary, wrapping within the text width. Line 3: the caption "Expires in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct" leading, and the "Reissue" text button trailing with a 44pt target.
- V4 · declined (fixture delta: Priya declined): the 16pt mail glyph; line 1 the recipient; line 2 a StatusChip "Declined · Thu 15 Oct". ⑥ holds only "Remove". No Resend.
- V5 · link-active: a 16pt link glyph; line 1 "Invite link" in bodySmall text.primary; line 2 the caption "Works once · Expires in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct". "Turn off link" is a trailing text button with a 44pt target. No overflow.
- V6 · awaiting-approval (Priya joined by link, so the link is used and no expiry applies): the 16pt mail glyph; line 1 "priya@example.com"; line 2 the caption "Waiting for your OK". "Approve" and "Remove" are equal-weight text buttons, trailing, 8dp apart, each with its own 44pt target. No overflow.

STATES (columns, in this order: S1, SF, S2, S3)
- S1 · default.
- SF · focused: the ring on the Resend button only.
- S2 · sending: "Resend" becomes "Sending…" and "Reissue" becomes "Reissuing…", each with a 12pt spinner before it (dark: D6; static text under Reduce Motion). Not re-tappable.
  - Follow-on (V1 only): inside the V1·S2 cell, under the sending row, draw a second stacked frame sub-labelled "then": the caption gains " · Sent" at the end and the button returns to "Resend". "Sent" is a role=status region whose accessible text is "Invitation resent". It stays one cell.
- S3 · offline: each action is disabled per R8, with a reason under it that names it: "You're offline. You can <resend | reissue | turn off the link | approve | remove this> when you're back." The ⑥ overflow stays enabled and opens; Cancel and Extend inside it are disabled with "You're offline. You can change this invite when you're back." On V4, Remove inside it uses the remove reason.

GRID CELLS (02 and 05; 14 cells)
- S1: V1, V1u, V2, V3, V4, V5, V6 (7).
- SF: V1 (1).
- S2: V1 with its "then" frame, and V3 (2). V4 in S2: "n/a — declined invites cannot be resent" (1).
- S3: V1, V5, and V6 with both buttons disabled, each with its own reason (3).
- Every other position stays empty canvas.

DARK (05): rows on dark surface.base. The V3 warning glyph keeps its hue (D7), captioned "warning on dark base 5.60:1". StatusChip fill uses D4. Spinners use D6. Add the Increase Contrast caption (R5).

AX5 / 200% (03): draw V1 and V6 in both columns. The recipient wraps at the "@". Captions wrap at middots. Resend drops below the caption and keeps its target. The overflow stays top-trailing (an icon button, not a text action). Approve and Remove stack below the caption, each full width with its own target.

GREYSCALE (03 captions): expiring = "Expires tomorrow · Mon 26 Oct" words · needs reissue = warning glyph shape + "Needs reissue" · declined = chip word "Declined" · link = link glyph + "Works once" · sending = "Sending…" words.

ACCESSIBILITY (panel)
- Pattern: "Invitation to priya@example.com, member, expires in 7 days, Monday 26 October. Resend. Button."
- A successful resend is announced as "Invitation resent" (the visible word is "Sent").
- Expiry is always in words. Targets are 44pt / 48dp / 44px with 8dp gaps.
- Overflow items are also custom actions. Disabled offline actions stay in the tree with their reason as a hint.

COPY RULES (panel)
- The expiry is shown on every pending invite (including expiring and needs-reissue rows) and on every active link. The awaiting-approval row shows none, because its link is already used.
- Dates show the weekday; beyond tomorrow, the relative count comes first: "in 7 days · Mon 26 Oct".
- The link warning ("Works once") appears at the point of choice.
- Every email uses @example.com. Each offline reason names the action it blocks.

PLATFORMS (panel): No platform differences.

INSTEAD OF (panel)
- Instead of a "Remind them" action on a declined invite, draw only "Remove". A decline is an answer.
- Instead of a real email domain, draw @example.com.
- Instead of a warning-tinted expiring row, draw the expiry in text.secondary words. Urgency comes from the date, not colour.

IN CONTEXT (04): three crops (R13).
1. f3-members-roster · ios, viewer Maya: the PENDING group with V1 and V5, below the MEMBERS group outline.
2. f3-invite-banner · android: V3 as the banner's single slot.
3. f3-invite-composer · web-1440: V5 under the link choice. "Turn off link" is visible, so there is no row menu button.

- Notes only (not in the grid): the Reissue and V4 Remove offline reasons, and the Cancel · Extend offline reason.
- Fixture deltas: V2 on Sun 25 Oct · V4 Priya declined · V6 Priya joined by link and awaits approval.

PUBLISH NAME: NotificationRow. This message is the complete NotificationRow specification.

PURPOSE (print at the top of 01). The in-app twin of every push. Tapping it lands on the exact object.

USED IN (panel): f3-household-notifications · f4-notification-settings.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw V1 (unread) and V4 (unread, system) at 2x, stacked, and V7 expanded beside them.
① Row: minimum 64pt on surface.base; padding 12pt vertical, 16pt leading (before the dot column) and 16pt trailing. The whole row is the target: draw its dashed target.
② A fixed 12pt leading column holding a 6pt unread dot in primary.700 (dark: D6), labelled "Unread". Read rows keep the empty column, so text never shifts. The dot is not a provenance mark and not a target.
③ A 28pt initials avatar: surface.sunken circle, initials in label 13/18 text.strong (dark: D4). System rows have no avatar; their text keeps the same leading alignment.
④ Line 1: body 16/24 text.primary, a sentence with the actor first.
⑤ Line 2: caption 12/16 text.secondary, joined by middots: date and time · home label (only for readers with more than one home) · for reminders, a trailing ProvenanceMark S.
⑥ Grouped row: a chevron disclosure that expands to the individual rows. The chevron is part of the row target. Expanded rows have no avatar, are indented to the text column, and each has line 2 "Today · 5:40 PM".
⑦ Web menu callout: "no custom actions; no row menu button".

VARIANTS (rows; label each "<code> · <key>"). Home A, viewer Maya, today Mon 19 Oct. Each variant is an independent specimen. Times are invented; 7:00 AM is assumed to be the morning briefing time.
- V1 · bill-paid: Sam avatar · "Sam marked Clark Public Utilities paid · $142.18" · "Today · 5:40 PM".
- V2 · task-completed: Sam avatar · "Sam marked "Carts out" done" · "Today · 5:55 PM".
- V3 · event-created: Sam avatar · "Sam added a date: Gutter cleaning, in 19 days · Sat 7 Nov" · "Yesterday · 8:12 PM".
- V4 · date-reminder (system): "Online or mail voter registration must arrive in 7 days · by Mon 26 Oct" · "Today · 7:00 AM" · filled mark.
- V5 · bill-reminder (system): "Clark Public Utilities is due in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct · $142.18" · "Today · 7:00 AM" · YOU ADDED mark.
- V6j · member-joined (fixture delta: Priya accepted): Priya avatar · "Priya joined Larkspur Loop — can see the calendar and bills" · "Today · 4:20 PM".
- V6l · member-left (fixture delta: Sam left): Sam avatar · "Sam left Larkspur Loop" · "Today · 4:25 PM".
- V7 · grouped: Sam avatar · "Sam marked 3 bills paid" · "Today · 5:40 PM" · chevron. Grid cells draw it collapsed; only 01 shows it expanded into three rows (Clark Public Utilities $142.18, City of Vancouver water $84.00, Comcast $79.99).
- V8 · gone-target: the landing after tapping a removed bill: the bill screen's header outline with a visible Back, and a plain body line "That bill was removed." in the bill's slot. Back returns to the notifications list.
- V9 · multi-home (fixture delta: Maya has a second home): V1 with line 2 "Today · 5:40 PM · Larkspur Loop".

STATES (columns, in this order: S1, S2, SF, S3, S4, SL)
- S1 · unread: dot present.
- S2 · read: no dot; identical text weight and fill.
- SF · focused: the ring on the whole row.
- S3 · push-off: a banner row at the top of the list, minimum 44pt: "Push is off. You'll still see these here. · Turn on", bodySmall text.strong on surface.sunken (dark: D3). The text wraps; "Turn on" stays trailing as a text button in primary.700 (5.39:1 on sunken; dark: dark border.focus, 6.83:1 on raised). An unread V1 sits under it.
- S4 · offline: the FreshnessLine "You're offline · as of 5:52 PM" above the list. Rows stay readable and unread. Tapping a row whose object is not cached shows "You're offline. This opens when you're back." under that row.
- SL · landing: the column for V8 only, which has no unread state.

GRID CELLS (02 and 05; 21 cells)
- S1 and S2: V1, V2, V3, V4, V5, V6j, V6l, V7 collapsed (16).
- S1: V9 (1). SF: V1 (1).
- S3: V1 row: the banner above an unread V1 (1).
- S4: V1 row: the FreshnessLine above unread V1 and V4, with the reason under V4 (1).
- SL: V8 (1).
- Every other position stays empty canvas.

DARK (05): rows on dark surface.base. Unread dot D6, avatars D4, S3 banner D3 with "Turn on" in dark border.focus, marks in dark text.secondary. Add the Increase Contrast caption (R5).

AX5 / 200% (03): draw V1 and V7 (collapsed) in both columns. The sentence wraps fully; line 2 wraps at middots. The dot column stays 12pt, top-aligned with line 1. The avatar stays 28pt. The V7 chevron moves below the text and stays part of the row target.

GREYSCALE (03): captions: unread = dot presence + "Unread" spoken first · reminder provenance = mark shape · grouped = chevron + "3 bills". Add one extra cell: an unread V1 above a read V1, differing only by the dot, captioned "unread is also spoken first".

COPY RULES (panel)

INSTEAD OF (panel)

Component 00c-08: TextActionRow. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PUBLISH NAME: TextActionRow. This message is the complete TextActionRow specification.

PURPOSE (print at the top of 01). Tertiary actions that spread the product: share, compare and outbound links. They never outrank the primary action.

USED IN (panel): f8-native-share-compare · f8-compare-sheet · f8-seasonal-aha · f6-place-section-details · f8-compare-reveal.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw V1 at 2x, and V2b at 2x below it.
① Two text buttons side by side: "Share this address" and "Compare with a friend". Each is bodySmallMedium primary.700 (dark: dark border.focus), with a 44pt / 48dp / 44px target, 8dp apart, no fill and no border. Draw both dashed targets and the 8dp gap.
② Caption under the buttons: caption 12/16 text.secondary, "The card shows your city and your readings — never your address, and no name."
③ Outbound variant: a bordered row, 48pt minimum, radius md 8, padding 12pt vertical and 16pt horizontal, with a 1px text.secondary edge (4.83:1 on base; a border token would fail as the only edge). It holds the destination text in bodySmall text.primary and a trailing 16pt external-link glyph "↗" in text.secondary. The whole row is the target. The "↗" at the end of each variant string below is this glyph: draw it once, as a vector, not as a text character.
④ Web menu callout: "no custom actions; no row menu button".

VARIANTS (rows; label each "<code> · <key>")
- V1 · share-compare: ① plus ②.
- V2a · outbound-test-kits: "Free test kits · Washington Dept of Health ↗".
- V2b · outbound-votewa: "Check or update at VoteWA ↗".

STATES (columns, in this order: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, SF)
- S1 · idle.
- S2 · minting: on "Compare with a friend", a 12pt spinner (dark: D6) replaces the start of the label, which reads "Making a link…". Not re-tappable. Under Reduce Motion the spinner is removed and the words stay.
- S3 · copied: the caption "Link copied" (role=status) sits between the buttons and the ② caption, and stays until the user leaves the screen.
- S4 · cancelled: nothing changes. Draw the idle row again with the annotation "share sheet dismissed: neutral, no message".
- S5 · offline: "Compare with a friend" is disabled per R8, with the reason "You're offline. Compare needs a connection." "Share this address" stays enabled (the system share sheet works offline). Outbound rows are disabled: the destination text turns text.secondary (glyph unchanged), the edge stays, and "You're offline. You can open this when you're back." sits under the row.
- SF · focused: the ring 2px outside the V2b row.

GRID CELLS (02 and 05; 16 cells)
- V1: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5 (5).
- V2a and V2b: S1 and S5 (4).
- V2a and V2b in S2, S3 and S4: "n/a — outbound links open the browser" (6).
- V2b: SF (1).

DARK (05): rows on dark surface.base. Buttons use dark border.focus. The outbound edge is a 1px dark text.secondary keyline (6.96:1 on dark base). Spinners use D6. Add the Increase Contrast caption (R5).

AX5 / 200% (03): draw V1 and V2b in both columns. The two buttons stack, each full width with its own target. The caption wraps. The outbound row wraps its destination text; the glyph stays trailing, top-aligned.

GREYSCALE (03 captions): actions = verbs and position, not colour · outbound = text.secondary edge + destination name + ↗ glyph · minting = "Making a link…" words · copied = "Link copied" words · offline = reason captions.

ACCESSIBILITY (panel)
- Links name their destination: "Check or update at VoteWA, opens in browser".
- "Link copied" is a status message.
- Targets are 44pt / 48dp / 44px, with 8dp between the two buttons.
- The minting button is announced as "Making a link" and cannot be re-activated.
- Disabled offline controls stay in the tree with their reason as a hint.

COPY RULES (panel)
- The V1 buttons start with a verb. Outbound rows name the destination as the contract gives it.
- The caption states what the card reveals.
- Use "Compare with a friend", never "challenge" or "vs".
- Offline reasons open with "You're offline".

PLATFORMS (panel)
- Only the system share sheet is used. iOS supplies LPLinkMetadata; Android supplies EXTRA_TITLE to the system chooser; web uses the browser's share, falling back to copying the link (S3).
- System UI is never redrawn by us: in 04 it is a surface.sunken frame with a 1px text.secondary keyline, labelled "system UI" in caption text.secondary.

INSTEAD OF (panel)
- Instead of placing these actions inside the sticky WallBar, draw them on the page surface under the content card. The wall's single primary action must stay single.
- Instead of an app-drawn Android chooser, draw the system chooser frame.
- Instead of filled or bordered buttons for share and compare, draw text buttons, so they never outrank the primary.

Component 00c-09: LockedActionRow. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PUBLISH NAME: LockedActionRow. This message is the complete LockedActionRow specification.

PURPOSE (print at the top of 01). Replaces or accompanies an unavailable control. It states the reason and the path forward.

USED IN (panel): f3b-locked-action-row · f3-members-roster · f3-member-home-dashboard · f3b-invitation-decision · f3-bills-list · f3-bill-detail-web · f3-household-calendar · f10-bill-provenance · f10-extraction-confirm · x-place-file · x-date-sheet · f6-home-basics-rows · f9-block-founders-panel · f11-keeper-strip.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw V1 at 2x: the disabled button with the row under it.
① One row, minimum 44pt, padding 12pt vertical and 16pt horizontal.
② Leading glyph, 16pt, text.secondary: a lock on every row except V4, which uses a clock.
③ Reason in bodySmall 14/20: text.strong on surface.sunken, or text.secondary on surface.base.
④ Trailing link "Verify address" in bodySmallMedium primary.700 (dark: dark border.focus), with a 44pt target. Draw its dashed target.
⑤ A 1px border.subtle hairline above the row (decoration only).
⑥ The reason wraps to 2 lines before anything truncates.
⑦ When the row sits under a disabled button, tapping the disabled button opens the same reason. Draw a callout arrow from the button to the row.
⑧ Web menu callout: "no custom actions; no row menu button".

VARIANTS (rows; label each "<code> · <key>")
- V1 · under-cta: a disabled filled button "Message your neighbors", 44pt / 48dp / 44px high, radius md, full content width (per R8: surface.sunken fill, text.strong label, kept focusable; dark: D4), with the row directly below it on surface.base: "Address verification needed to message your neighbors · Verify address".
- V2 list row (group heading only, not a grid row): "Address verification needed to get a residency letter · Verify address", drawn as two rows:
  - V2s · list-row-sunken: on surface.sunken, reason in text.strong.
  - V2b · list-row-base: on surface.base, reason in text.secondary.
- V3 · card-header: a card (radius lg, shadow sm; dark: D8 edge) titled "Residency Pass", with the row inside the header on surface.base: "Address verification needed to show your Residency Pass · Verify address".
- V4 · pending (viewer Sam, whose postcard is still in transit; Maya's address is already confirmed): a 16pt clock glyph in text.secondary instead of the lock, then "We're checking your postcard code — expected in 3–10 days · Thu 22–Thu 29 Oct", with no link.
- V5 · server-refused, shown after a tap the server refused: "Address verification needed to get a residency letter. We checked again. · Verify address".
- V6 · names-who-can-act (viewer Sam, who can see bills but not add them): "Maya can add bills here", with no link.
- V7 · not-at-tier (Place B): the lock glyph, then "Claim this address first" in text.secondary, with no link and no button.
All rows sit on surface.base unless stated.

STATES (columns, in this order: S1, SF, S2, S3; each ends with its 03 greyscale caption)
- S1 · locked. Greyscale: "locked = lock glyph + the words; nothing is coloured except the link, which reads through its position and its verb".
- SF · focused: the ring on the "Verify address" link only (R8). Greyscale: "focused = ring".
- S2 · pending: V4's form. Greyscale: "pending = clock glyph + 'We're checking' words".
- S3 · offline: the link is disabled per R8 (text.secondary, focusable). The row grows: the caption "You're offline. You can verify when you're back." sits under the reason text, at the leading edge, full width. On V1 the button stays as in S1; its reason is still the row itself, and the button gets no offline caption. Greyscale: "offline = the dimmed link + the offline caption under the reason".

GRID CELLS (02 and 05; 17 cells)
- S1: V1, V2s, V2b, V3, V5, V6 and V7 (7 cells). V4 in S1: "n/a — pending is its own variant" (1 cell).
- SF: V2b (1 cell).
- S2: V4 (1 cell).
- S3: V1, V2b, V3 and V5 (4 cells). V4, V6 and V7 in S3: "n/a — this variant has no link to disable" (3 cells).

DARK (05)
- V2s uses D3 (dark raised, dark text.strong). The V1 disabled button uses D4. The V3 card uses D8: caption "keyline 5.71:1" beside it. Other rows sit on dark base with dark text.secondary reasons (6.96:1).
- The lock and clock glyphs use dark text.secondary. Links use dark border.focus.
- Add the Increase Contrast caption (R5).

AX5 / 200% (03): draw V1 and V2b in both columns.
- The reason wraps fully.
- "Verify address" drops to its own line below the reason, left-aligned, keeping its target.
- The glyph scales to 24pt and stays top-aligned.
- The V1 button grows in height and its label wraps.

ACCESSIBILITY (panel)
- The reason is at 4.5:1 or better (text.strong on sunken 9.37:1; text.secondary on base 4.83:1).
- The link names its destination: "Verify address, opens Verify this address".
- The disabled button is exposed with its reason as a hint: "Message your neighbors, dimmed. Address verification needed to message your neighbors."
- The offline link is exposed as dimmed, with its reason as a hint.
- Row and link targets are 44pt / 48dp / 44px.

COPY RULES (panel)
- The pattern is "Address verification needed to <specific action>". Any extra context (V5) follows as a second sentence.
- Never write a generic "Verification required".
- When someone else can act, name them ("Maya can add bills here").
- Dates beyond tomorrow carry the relative count (V4).

PLATFORMS (panel): No platform differences.

INSTEAD OF (panel)

- Instead of a present but inert control with no explanation, draw the control with this row under it.
- Instead of an "Address verification needed…" reason for a saved-place user on a home-only feature, draw V7 "Claim this address first". Verification means nothing before a claim.

PUBLISH NAME: GrantLimitList. This message is the complete GrantLimitList specification.

PURPOSE (print at the top of 01). Two scannable lists: what you get now (ticked) and what needs address verification (locked). One component serves invite, attestation and verify.

USED IN (panel): f3b-invitation-decision · f3-invite-composer · f3b-owner-attestation · f3b-verify-address-sheet · f9-verification-promise-copy · f3-members-roster.

EXTRA STAND-IN FOR THIS COMPONENT (label it "stand-in", per R11)
- ChoiceChip: pill, 32pt visual height inside a 44pt / 48dp target, label 13/18. Selected: primary.50 fill, primary.700 label and a leading check glyph (dark: D5). Unselected: a 1px text.secondary edge and a text.strong label. The focus ring is distinct from selection. At AX sizes the chips become radio rows. Platform notes: an iOS segmented control where native; M3 filter chips on Android.

STRING SET (exact; every variant draws from it)
- Grants: "Sees and edits the calendar" · "Sees bills and who paid" · "Sees who lives here".
- Limits: "Message your neighbors" · "Get a residency letter" · "Show your Residency Pass" · "Share what you pay in rent (Real Rent)" · "Earn a Block Founder rank".

ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw the specimen twice: the stacked iOS form of V1 at 2x, and the two-column web-1440 form of V1 beside or below it at 1x (never shrunk; R2).
① Grant list heading "What you get now": label 13/18 text.strong. The grant list always comes first.
② Grant rows, 44pt each: a 16pt bare stroke check in success hue (a stroke, not a disc, so it cannot be mistaken for the YOU ADDED mark; dark: D7), a 12pt gap, and the verb phrase in body 16/24 text.primary.
③ Limit list heading "What needs address verification": label 13/18 text.strong.
④ Limit rows, 44pt each: a 16pt lock glyph in text.secondary, a 12pt gap, and the verb phrase in body 16/24 text.primary.
⑤ Callout: "both lists use identical type and row height".
⑥ Callout: "two columns 24pt apart on web 1440; stacked on mobile (iOS, Android, web 390)".
⑦ Callout: "one shared string set; every variant draws from it".
⑧ Web menu callout: "no custom actions; no row menu button".

VARIANTS (rows; label each "<code> · <key>")
- V1 · invitation-decision: both headings, all 3 grants and all 5 limits. The grid cell draws the stacked iOS form.
- V2 · role-offered: under a 44pt disclosure row "Role offered: Member" (expanded), the heading "What you get now" and the 3 grants only.
- V3 · attestation (viewer Maya, the owner, confirming that Sam lives here): the heading "What Sam gets once you confirm", then 3 rows with stroke checks: "Message your neighbors" · "Get a residency letter" · "Show your Residency Pass". V3 uses the grant row style because these become Sam's grants once Maya confirms; the heading carries the condition.
- V4 · verify-unlock: the heading "What needs address verification", then "Message your neighbors" · "Get a residency letter" with lock glyphs, then a 44pt row "Show 3 more" with a chevron that expands the remaining three limits.
- V5 · role-caption-member: a ChoiceChip pair, "Member" (selected) and "Guest". Under them, a caption in caption 12/16 text.secondary: "Sees and edits the calendar · Sees bills and who paid · Sees who lives here". It has no visible heading and is exposed as a list with the accessible name "What members can do".
- V5g · role-caption-guest: the same chips with "Guest" selected. The caption reads "Sees and edits the calendar", exposed as a list named "What guests can do".

STATES (columns, in this order: S1, SF, S2)
- S1 · default.
- SF · focused: on V4, the ring on the "Show 3 more" row only. On V5, the focus ring on the unselected "Guest" chip, with "Member" still selected (fill and check). On V5g, the focus ring on the unselected "Member" chip, with "Guest" still selected. So V5·S1 sits beside V5·SF, and V5g·S1 beside V5g·SF, in the same row.
- S2 · accepted: the limit list gains the caption "Verify your address to unlock these", in caption text.secondary, directly under its heading.

GRID CELLS (02 and 05; 15 cells)
- S1: V1, V2, V3, V4, V5 and V5g (6 cells).
- SF: V4, V5 and V5g (3 cells).
- S2: V1 (1 cell). V2, V3, V4, V5 and V5g in S2: "n/a — accepted applies after an invitation is accepted" (5 cells).

DARK (05)
- Lists sit on dark surface.base. The success check keeps its hue (D7): caption "success on dark base 4.74:1" beside the first one. Lock glyphs use dark text.secondary.
- Selected chips use D5. Unselected chip edges use dark text.secondary (6.96:1).
- Add the Increase Contrast caption (R5).

AX5 / 200% (03): draw V1 and V5 in both columns.
- The two lists stack, grants first.
- Phrases wrap; glyphs stay top-aligned and scale to 24pt.
- In V5, the chips become radio rows, each with a 44pt / 48dp target, and the caption wraps under them.

GREYSCALE (03 captions)
- grant vs limit = stroke check vs lock (shape) + the headings.
- selected chip = its check glyph.
- focused = ring.
- accepted = the "Verify your address to unlock these" caption.

ACCESSIBILITY (panel)
- Each list has a heading, exposed as a heading. Where there is no visible heading (V5, V5g), the list has an accessible name.
- The check and lock glyphs are decorative; the heading carries the meaning.
- Rows are read as list items: "What you get now, list, 3 items. Sees and edits the calendar."
- "Show 3 more" is a 44pt / 48dp / 44px button, spoken "Show 3 more" (the spoken name matches the visible label).
- Chips are spoken with their selected state: "Member, selected".

COPY RULES (panel)
- Every row is a verb phrase.
- Use the string set exactly.
- Never write a bare product name.

PLATFORMS (panel): stacked on mobile (iOS, Android, web 390) and two columns on web 1440. The V5 chips follow the ChoiceChip platform notes (an iOS segmented control where native; M3 filter chips on Android).

INSTEAD OF (panel)
- Instead of a warning box around the limits, draw the plain lock rows. Limits are information, not danger.
- Instead of bare product names ("Real Rent", "Residency Pass"), draw verb phrases ("Share what you pay in rent (Real Rent)"). People decide on what they can do.
- Instead of text.muted on sunken for locked rows, draw body text.primary with a text.secondary lock, because these rows must be read.

Component 00c-11: InlineErrorRow. Follow the board rules from the setup message.

PUBLISH NAME: InlineErrorRow. This message is the complete InlineErrorRow specification.

PURPOSE (print at the top of 01). Shows a partial failure in one component. It names what failed and keeps everything else live.

USED IN (panel): f1-today-tab · f1-claim-receipt · f10-mail-day-triage · f10-snap-capture-tray · f10-bill-trend · f4-briefing-optin-card · f4-notification-settings · f6-home-basics-rows · f11-keeper-naming · f11-keeper-strip.

ANATOMY (01-anatomy)
Draw V1 at 2x, sitting in the slot of an air section between two live section outlines. Beside it, draw V4 at 2x.
① The row sits in the failed component's own slot and height, and keeps its position in the list. Minimum 44pt, padding 12pt vertical and 16pt horizontal.
② Leading glyph, 16pt: an exclamation mark in a circle, in error hue (glyph only; dark: D7).
③ Message: bodySmall 14/20, text.primary.
④ Trailing "Retry" text button: bodySmallMedium primary.700 (dark: dark border.focus), 44pt target. Draw its dashed target.
⑤ Surface: surface.base. It is errorBg only when a write failed (V4; dark: D2). On errorBg, nothing uses text.secondary (R4). The error-on-errorBg pair is not in the R6 table, so write the measured caption "error on errorBg 4.41:1" beside the V4 glyph.
⑥ Web menu callout: "no custom actions; no row menu button".

VARIANTS (rows; label each "<code> · <key>")
- V1 · provider-unreachable: "We couldn't reach AirNow just now · Retry".
- V2 · carry-failed: "We couldn't move your water-heater warranty · Retry".
- V3 · upload-failed: "Upload failed · Retry".
- V4 · save-failed, on errorBg, value preserved: above the row, the field it belongs to still shows "Pickup day" with the value "Tuesday" and a hollow ProvenanceMark (the confirm did not save). Maya tapped Tuesday to confirm the city schedule and the save failed. The row reads "We couldn't save your pickup day. Your choice is still here. · Retry".
- V5 · fail-closed: draw an f9-block-founders-panel card (radius lg; dark: D8 edge) with its title "Block Founders" and a LockedActionRow in its card-header form directly under the title ("Address verification needed to earn a Block Founder rank · Verify address"). The founding meter, the invite banner and the Earn row are absent, with no gap and no error row. Outside the card, draw dashed annotation brackets where each would have been, labelled "founding meter", "invite banner" and "Earn row", plus the annotation "fail-closed: nothing rendered, no error row".

STATES (columns, in this order: S1, SF, S2)
- S1 · failed.
- SF · focused: the ring on "Retry" only.
- S2 · retrying: "Retry" becomes "Retrying…" in bodySmallMedium (text.secondary on base, text.strong on errorBg), with a 12pt primary.700 spinner before it (dark: D6), or the static text under Reduce Motion. It is not re-tappable. The target stays in place and the message stays.

GRID CELLS (02 and 05; 11 cells)
- S1: V1, V2, V3, V4 and V5 (5 cells). The V4 cell carries the caption "error on errorBg 4.41:1" beside its glyph.
- SF: V1 (1 cell).
- S2: V1, V2, V3 and V4 (4 cells). V5 in S2: "n/a — nothing to retry" (1 cell).

DARK (05)
- V1–V3 sit on dark surface.base; the error glyph keeps its hue (D7): caption "error on dark base 3.70:1" beside the first one.
- V4 uses D2 (dark raised plus a 1.5px error border); its glyph measures 3.03:1 on dark raised, so caption that too.
- V5's card uses D8: caption "keyline 5.71:1". Its LockedActionRow follows its own dark rules (dark text.secondary reason, dark border.focus link).
- Spinners use D6. Add the Increase Contrast caption (R5).

AX5 / 200% (03): draw V1 and V4 in both columns.
- The message wraps.
- "Retry" drops below it, on its own line, and keeps its target.
- The glyph scales with the text and stays top-aligned.
- V4's field above keeps "Tuesday" and its hollow mark visible.

GREYSCALE (03 captions)
- failure = glyph shape (exclamation in a circle) + the words.
- V4 = the words and the kept "Tuesday"; errorBg is not needed to understand it.
- focused = ring.
- retrying = "Retrying…" words.
- fail-closed = absence, carried by the annotations.

ACCESSIBILITY (panel)
- A polite live-region announcement when the row appears.
- Retry names its target: V1 "Retry air quality"; V2 "Retry moving your water-heater warranty"; V3 "Retry upload"; V4 "Retry saving pickup day".
- Retry targets are 44pt / 48dp / 44px.
- The retrying state is announced as "Retrying".
- V5 announces nothing, because nothing is rendered.

COPY RULES (panel)
- Messages are specific and blameless.
- Name the source or the thing that failed, and say what to do next.
- Typed and chosen input is kept.

PLATFORMS (panel): No platform differences.

INSTEAD OF (panel)
- Instead of "Oops, something went wrong", draw "We couldn't reach AirNow just now · Retry". The user needs to know what failed.
- Instead of hiding a failed row among successful ones or dropping it, draw it in its own slot and order, so nothing silently disappears.
- Instead of an error row for a fail-closed component, draw nothing. A broken meter must never promise a slot.
- Instead of clearing the field on a failed save, keep "Tuesday" in it.

IN CONTEXT (04): three crops (R13).
1. f1-today-tab · ios, Home A: ScopeChip "Your household"; the pickup section above, still live, with its hollow mark (the confirm in crop 3 did not save); the air section replaced by V1; the legend line.

3. f6-home-basics-rows · web-390, Home A: ScopeChip "Your household"; V4 under its "Pickup day" field, which shows "Tuesday" with a hollow mark; the legend line.

Below it, a visible action row of three text buttons, each with a 44pt / 48dp target, 8dp apart: "Retake" · "Delete" · "Same letter as previous". Draw their dashed targets.
